2.45.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
evaṃ ṣoḍaśa dānāni kathitāni śubhāni ca /
jīvacchrā ddhakramo 'smākaṃ vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam //
2.45.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
एवं षोडश दानानि कथितानि शुभानि च ।
जीवच्छ्रा द्धक्रमो ऽस्माकं वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥
2.45.m: The sages said: / In this manner the sixteen auspicious gifts have been described. / You should now describe to us the procedure of the funeral rite performed while alive.

2.45.s:
sūta uvāca
jīvacchrāddhavidhiṃ vakṣye samāsātsarvasaṃmatam /
manave devadevena kathitaṃ brahmaṇā purā //
2.45.d:
सूत उवाच
जीवच्छ्राद्धविधिं वक्ष्ये समासात्सर्वसंमतम् ।
मनवे देवदेवेन कथितं ब्रह्मणा पुरा ॥
2.45.m: Sūta said: / I shall concisely state the procedure of the funeral rite performed while alive, accepted by all, / which was formerly told to Manu by the god of gods, Brahmā,

2.45.s:
vasiṣṭhāsa ca śiṣṭāya bhṛgave bhārgavāya ca /
śṛṇvantu sarvabhāvena sarvasiddhikaraṃ param //
2.45.d:
वसिष्ठास च शिष्टाय भृगवे भार्गवाय च ।
शृण्वन्तु सर्वभावेन सर्वसिद्धिकरं परम् ॥
2.45.m: and to Vasiṣṭha, to the disciplined [sage], and to Bhṛgu the Bhārgava. / Listen with wholehearted devotion to this supreme [rite] that grants all accomplishments,

2.45.s:
śrāddhamārgakramaṃ sākṣācchrāddhārhāṇāmapi kramam /
viśeṣamapi vakṣyāmi jīvacchrāddhasya suvratāḥ //
2.45.d:
श्राद्धमार्गक्रमं साक्षाच्छ्राद्धार्हाणामपि क्रमम् ।
विशेषमपि वक्ष्यामि जीवच्छ्राद्धस्य सुव्रताः ॥
2.45.m: the sequence of the path of funeral rites, the proper order of those eligible for funeral rites directly, / and also the distinctive features of the funeral rite performed while alive, O men of noble vows.

2.45.s:
parvate vā nadītīre vane vāyatane 'pi vā /
jīvacchrāddhaṃ prakartavyaṃ mṛtakāle prayatnataḥ //
2.45.d:
पर्वते वा नदीतीरे वने वायतने ऽपि वा ।
जीवच्छ्राद्धं प्रकर्तव्यं मृतकाले प्रयत्नतः ॥
2.45.m: On a mountain, or on a riverbank, in a forest, or in a temple, / the funeral rite performed while alive should be diligently performed at the time of [anticipated] death.

2.45.s:
jīvacchrāddhe kṛte jīvo jīvanneva vimucyate /
karma kurvannakurvanvā jñānī vājñānavānapi //
2.45.d:
जीवच्छ्राद्धे कृते जीवो जीवन्नेव विमुच्यते ।
कर्म कुर्वन्नकुर्वन्वा ज्ञानी वाज्ञानवानपि ॥
2.45.m: When the funeral rite performed while alive has been performed, the soul is liberated while still living— / whether performing ritual action or not, whether possessing spiritual knowledge or lacking it,

2.45.s:
śrotriyo 'śrotriyo vāpi brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo 'pi vā /
vaiśyo vā nātra saṃdeho yogamārgagato yatā //
2.45.d:
श्रोत्रियो ऽश्रोत्रियो वापि ब्राह्मणः क्षत्रियो ऽपि वा ।
वैश्यो वा नात्र संदेहो योगमार्गगतो यता ॥
2.45.m: whether learned in the Veda or not learned, whether a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, / or a vaiśya; there is no doubt here, as one who has entered upon the path of yoga.

2.45.s:
parīkṣya bhūmiṃ vidhivadgandhavarṇarasādibhiḥ /
śalyamuddhṛtya yatnena sthāṇḍilaṃ saikataṃ bhuvi //
2.45.d:
परीक्ष्य भूमिं विधिवद्गन्धवर्णरसादिभिः ।
शल्यमुद्धृत्य यत्नेन स्थाण्डिलं सैकतं भुवि ॥
2.45.m: Having examined the ground according to rule by its smell, colour, taste, and the rest, / and carefully removed any impurity, [one should prepare] a sandy altar on the ground.

2.45.s:
madhyato hastamātreṇa kuṇḍaṃ caivāyataṃ śubham /
sthāṇḍilaṃ vā prakartavyamiṣumātraṃ punaḥ punaḥ //
2.45.d:
मध्यतो हस्तमात्रेण कुण्डं चैवायतं शुभम् ।
स्थाण्डिलं वा प्रकर्तव्यमिषुमात्रं पुनः पुनः ॥
2.45.m: In the middle, an auspicious, oblong fire-pit measuring one cubit [should be made], / or an altar should be repeatedly made measuring an arrow's length.

2.45.s:
upalipya vidhānena cālipyāgniṃ vidhāya ca /
anvādhāya yathāśāstraṃ parigṛhya ca sarvataḥ //
2.45.d:
उपलिप्य विधानेन चालिप्याग्निं विधाय च ।
अन्वाधाय यथाशास्त्रं परिगृह्य च सर्वतः ॥
2.45.m: Having smeared it according to rule, decorated it, and established the fire, / having placed the fuel according to the sacred texts and enclosed it all around,

2.45.s:
paristīrya svaśākhoktaṃ pāraṃparyakramāgatam /
samāpyāgnimukhaṃ sarvaṃ mantrairetairyathākramam //
2.45.d:
परिस्तीर्य स्वशाखोक्तं पारंपर्यक्रमागतम् ।
समाप्याग्निमुखं सर्वं मन्त्रैरेतैर्यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.45.m: having strewn [sacred grass] as prescribed in one's own Vedic branch and handed down through unbroken lineage, / having concluded the entire beginning of the fire rite with these mantras in due order,

2.45.s:
saṃpūjya sthaṇḍile vahnau homayetsamidādibhiḥ /
ādau kṛtvā samiddhomaṃ caruṇā ca pṛthakpṛthak //
2.45.d:
संपूज्य स्थण्डिले वह्नौ होमयेत्समिदादिभिः ।
आदौ कृत्वा समिद्धोमं चरुणा च पृथक्पृथक् ॥
2.45.m: and having worshipped in the fire upon the altar, one should make oblations with firewood sticks and other [materials]. / Having first performed the offering of firewood sticks, then separately with sacrificial boiled rice,

2.45.s:
ghṛtena ca pṛthakprātre śodhitena pṛthakpṛthak /
juhuyādātmanoddhṛtya tattvabhūtāni sarvataḥ //
2.45.d:
घृतेन च पृथक्प्रात्रे शोधितेन पृथक्पृथक् ।
जुहुयादात्मनोद्धृत्य तत्त्वभूतानि सर्वतः ॥
2.45.m: and with clarified butter purified separately in a separate vessel, / one should offer oblations, offering up the constitutive principles and elements on every side:

2.45.d: महादेव सत्यं मे गोपाय श्रद्धां धर्मे महादेवाय ऋतं स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: O Mahādeva, protect my truth, my faith in righteousness; ṛtam, svāhā to Mahādeva!

2.45.s: mahādeva satyaṃ me gopāya śraddhāṃ dharme mahādevāya patnyai ṛtaṃ namaḥ //
2.45.d: महादेव सत्यं मे गोपाय श्रद्धां धर्मे महादेवाय पत्न्यै ऋतं नमः ॥
2.45.m: O Mahādeva, protect my truth, my faith in righteousness; ṛtam, homage to the consort of Mahādeva!

2.45.s: mahādeva satyaṃ ma gopāya śraddhāṃ mahādevasya patnyai ṛtaṃ svāhā //
2.45.d: महादेव सत्यं म गोपाय श्रद्धां महादेवस्य पत्न्यै ऋतं स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: O Mahādeva, protect my truth, my faith [in righteousness]; ṛtam, svāhā to the consort of Mahādeva!

2.45.s: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupataye devāya satyaṃ namaḥ //
2.45.d: पशुपते पाशं मे गोपाय भोक्तृत्वभोग्यं पशुपतये देवाय सत्यं नमः ॥
2.45.m: "O Paśupati, protect my fetter, the object of enjoyment and condition of being the experiencer! Truth to the god Paśupati, namaḥ!"

2.45.s: paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya bhoktṛtvabhāgyaṃ paśupataye devasya satyaṃ svāhā //
2.45.d: पशुपते पाशं मे गोपाय भोक्तृत्वभाग्यं पशुपतये देवस्य सत्यं स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: "O Paśupati, protect my fetter, the fortune of being the experiencer! Truth to the god Paśupati, svāhā!"

2.45.s: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ me gopāya yoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupater devasya patnyai satyaṃ namaḥ //
2.45.d: ओं पशुपते पाशं मे गोपाय योक्तृत्वभोग्यं पशुपतेर् देवस्य पत्न्यै सत्यं नमः ॥
2.45.m: "Oṃ, O Paśupati, protect my fetter, the object of enjoyment and condition of being the yoker! Truth to the wife of the god Paśupati, namaḥ!"

2.45.s: oṃ paśupate pāśaṃ ma gopāya yoktṛtvabhogyaṃ paśupaterdevasya patnyai satyaṃ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं पशुपते पाशं म गोपाय योक्तृत्वभोग्यं पशुपतेर्देवस्य पत्न्यै सत्यं स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: "Oṃ, O Paśupati, protect my fetter, the object of enjoyment and condition of being the yoker! Truth to the wife of the god Paśupati, svāhā!"

2.45.s: oṃ śivāya namaḥ //
2.45.d: ओं शिवाय नमः ॥

2.45.s: oṃ śivāya satyaṃ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं शिवाय सत्यं स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s:
evaṃ śivāya hotavyaṃ viriñcyādyaṃ ca pūvavat /
viriñcādyaṃ ca pūrvoktaṃ sṛṣṭimārgeṣu suvratāḥ //
2.45.d:
एवं शिवाय होतव्यं विरिञ्च्याद्यं च पूववत् ।
विरिञ्चाद्यं च पूर्वोक्तं सृष्टिमार्गेषु सुव्रताः ॥
2.45.m: Thus the offering should be made to Śiva, and as before beginning with Viriñca. / As mentioned before beginning with Viriñca, [offerings are made] according to the courses of creation, O you of noble vows.

2.45.s:
punaḥ paśupateḥ patnīṃ tathā paśupatīṃ kramāt /
saṃpūjya pūrvavanmantrairhetavyaṃ ca krameṇa vai //
2.45.d:
पुनः पशुपतेः पत्नीं तथा पशुपतीं क्रमात् ।
संपूज्य पूर्ववन्मन्त्रैर्हेतव्यं च क्रमेण वै ॥
2.45.m: Then, having worshipped in order the wife of Paśupati and likewise Paśupati as before, / oblations must indeed be offered sequentially with the mantras,

2.45.s: carvantamājyapūrvaṃ ca samidantaṃ samāhitaḥ //
2.45.d: चर्वन्तमाज्यपूर्वं च समिदन्तं समाहितः ॥
2.45.m: concentrated in mind, beginning with clarified butter, ending with the sacrificial cooked rice (caru), and ending with the fuel sticks.

2.45.s: oṃ śarva dharāṃ me chindhi ghrāṇe gandhaṃ chindhi meghaṃ jahi bhūḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं शर्व धरां मे छिन्धि घ्राणे गन्धं छिन्धि मेघं जहि भूः स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: "Oṃ Śarva, sever the earth for me; sever the smell in my nose; destroy the cloud; bhūḥ svāhā!"

2.45.s: bhuvaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: भुवः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s: svaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: स्वः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s: bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: भूर्भुवः स्वः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s:
evaṃ pṛthakpṛthagghutvā kevalena ghṛtena vā /
sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā //
2.45.d:
एवं पृथक्पृथग्घुत्वा केवलेन घृतेन वा ।
सहस्रं वा तदर्धं वा शतमष्टोत्तरं तु वा ॥
2.45.m: Having thus offered each separately, or with pure ghee, / one thousand times, or half of that, or one hundred and eight times,

2.45.s:
virajā ca ghṛtenaiva śatamaṣṭottaraṃ pṛthak /
prāṇādibhiśca juhuyāddhṛtenaiva tu kevalam //
2.45.d:
विरजा च घृतेनैव शतमष्टोत्तरं पृथक् ।
प्राणादिभिश्च जुहुयाद्धृतेनैव तु केवलम् ॥
2.45.m: and the Virajā [hymn] with ghee separately one hundred and eight times, / one should offer with [the mantras to] the prāṇas and others with pure ghee alone:

2.45.s: oṃ prāṇe niviṣṭo 'mṛtaṃ juhomi śivo ma viśāpradāhāya prāṇāya svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं प्राणे निविष्टो ऽमृतं जुहोमि शिवो म विशाप्रदाहाय प्राणाय स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: "Oṃ, entered into the out-breath (prāṇa), I offer nectar; O Śiva, enter into me without burning; to prāṇa svāhā!"

2.45.s: prāṇādhipataye rudrāya vṛṣāntakāya svāhā //
2.45.d: प्राणाधिपतये रुद्राय वृषान्तकाय स्वाहा ॥
2.45.m: "To Rudra, the lord of prāṇa, the ender of righteousness, svāhā!"

2.45.s: oṃ bhūḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं भूः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s: oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं भुवः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s: oṃ svaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: ओं स्वः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s: bhūrbhūvaḥ svaḥ svāhā //
2.45.d: भूर्भूवः स्वः स्वाहा ॥

2.45.s:
evaṃ krameṇa juhuyācchrāddhoktaṃ ca yatākramam /
saptame 'hani yogīndrāñ chrāddhārhān api bhojayet //
2.45.d:
एवं क्रमेण जुहुयाच्छ्राद्धोक्तं च यताक्रमम् ।
सप्तमे ऽहनि योगीन्द्राञ् छ्राद्धार्हान् अपि भोजयेत् ॥
2.45.m: One should offer in this sequence, and as prescribed for the ancestral rite (śrāddha) in proper order. / On the seventh day, one should feed foremost yogins who are worthy of the śrāddha,

2.45.s:
śarvādīnāṃ ca viprāṇāṃ vastrābharaṇakaṃbalān /
vāhanaṃ śayanaṃ yānaṃ kāṃsyatāmrādibhājanam //
2.45.d:
शर्वादीनां च विप्राणां वस्त्राभरणकंबलान् ।
वाहनं शयनं यानं कांस्यताम्रादिभाजनम् ॥
2.45.m: and [give] to the brāhmaṇas who represent Śarva and the others garments, ornaments, blankets, / a mount, a bed, a conveyance, bronze, copper and other vessels,

2.45.s:
haimaṃ ca rājataṃ dhenuṃ tilān kṣetraṃ ca vaibhavam /
dāsīdāsagaṇaścaiva dātavyo dakṣiṇāmapi //
2.45.d:
हैमं च राजतं धेनुं तिलान् क्षेत्रं च वैभवम् ।
दासीदासगणश्चैव दातव्यो दक्षिणामपि ॥
2.45.m: gold and silver, a cow, sesame seeds, land, and wealth; / a troop of female and male servants is to be given, as well as a priestly fee (dakṣiṇā).

2.45.s:
piṇḍaṃ ca pūrvavaddadyātpṛthagaṣṭaprakārataḥ /
brāhmaṇānaṃ sahasraṃ ca bhojayecca sadakṣiṇam //
2.45.d:
पिण्डं च पूर्ववद्दद्यात्पृथगष्टप्रकारतः ।
ब्राह्मणानं सहस्रं च भोजयेच्च सदक्षिणम् ॥
2.45.m: And one should offer the rice-ball (piṇḍa) as before, separately in eight ways, / and feed a thousand brāhmaṇas accompanied with priestly fees,

2.45.s:
ekaṃ vā yoganirataṃ bhasmaniṣṭhaṃ jitendriyam /
tryahaṃ caiva tu rudrasya mahācarunivedanam //
2.45.d:
एकं वा योगनिरतं भस्मनिष्ठं जितेन्द्रियम् ।
त्र्यहं चैव तु रुद्रस्य महाचरुनिवेदनम् ॥
2.45.m: or a single [brāhmaṇa] who is devoted to yoga, grounded in sacred ash, and has subdued his senses. / And for three days, there is the offering of the great caru to Rudra.

2.45.s:
viśeṣa evaṃ kathita aśeṣaśrāddhacoditaḥ /
mṛte kuryānna kuryādvā jīvanmukto yataḥ svayam //
2.45.d:
विशेष एवं कथित अशेषश्राद्धचोदितः ।
मृते कुर्यान्न कुर्याद्वा जीवन्मुक्तो यतः स्वयम् ॥
2.45.m: Thus the special procedure prescribed for the complete śrāddha has been spoken. / When dead, [his heirs] may perform it or may not perform it, since he is himself liberated while living (jīvanmukta).

2.45.s:
nityanaimittikādīni kuryāddhā saṃttyajettu vā /
bāndhave 'pi mṛte tasya śaucāśaucaṃ na vidyate //
2.45.d:
नित्यनैमित्तिकादीनि कुर्याद्धा संत्त्यजेत्तु वा ।
बान्धवे ऽपि मृते तस्य शौचाशौचं न विद्यते ॥
2.45.m: He may perform regular and occasional rites, or he may abandon them. / Even when a relative dies, for him there is neither ritual purity nor ritual impurity.

2.45.s:
sūtakaṃ ca na saṃdehaḥ snānamātreṇa śuddhyati /
paścājjāte kumāre ca sve kṣetre cātmano yadi //
2.45.d:
सूतकं च न संदेहः स्नानमात्रेण शुद्ध्यति ।
पश्चाज्जाते कुमारे च स्वे क्षेत्रे चात्मनो यदि ॥
2.45.m: And birth/death pollution—there is no doubt—is purified merely by bathing. / If a son is born later in his own wife,

2.45.s:
tasya sarvaṃ prakartavyaṃ putro 'pi brahmavidbhivet /
kanyakā yadi rāñjātā paścāttasya mahātmanaḥ //
2.45.d:
तस्य सर्वं प्रकर्तव्यं पुत्रो ऽपि ब्रह्मविद्भिवेत् ।
कन्यका यदि राञ्जाता पश्चात्तस्य महात्मनः ॥
2.45.m: everything is to be performed for him; the son too will become a knower of Brahman. / If a daughter is born later to that great-souled one,

2.45.s:
ekaparṇā iva jñeyā aparṇā iva suvratā /
bhavatyeva na saṃdehastasyāścānvayajā api //
2.45.d:
एकपर्णा इव ज्ञेया अपर्णा इव सुव्रता ।
भवत्येव न संदेहस्तस्याश्चान्वयजा अपि ॥
2.45.m: she should be known as like Ekaparṇā, like Aparṇā, O you of noble vows; / she indeed becomes [so], there is no doubt, and her descendants also

2.45.s:
mucyante nātra saṃdehaḥ pitaro narakādapi /
mucyante karmaṇānena mātṛtaḥ pitṛtastathā //
2.45.d:
मुच्यन्ते नात्र संदेहः पितरो नरकादपि ।
मुच्यन्ते कर्मणानेन मातृतः पितृतस्तथा ॥
2.45.m: are liberated, there is no doubt of this, and the ancestors even from hell / are liberated through this rite, from the maternal side as well as from the paternal side.

2.45.s:
kālaṃ gate dvije bhūmau khaneccāpi dahettu vā /
putrakṛtyamaśeṣaṃ ca kṛtvā doṣo na vidyate //
2.45.d:
कालं गते द्विजे भूमौ खनेच्चापि दहेत्तु वा ।
पुत्रकृत्यमशेषं च कृत्वा दोषो न विद्यते ॥
2.45.m: When the twice-born has passed away, one may bury him in the earth or cremate him; / having performed all the filial duties, no fault is incurred.

2.45.s:
karmaṇā cottareṇaiva gatirasya na vidyate /
brahmaṇākathitaṃ sarvaṃ munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām //
2.45.d:
कर्मणा चोत्तरेणैव गतिरस्य न विद्यते ।
ब्रह्मणाकथितं सर्वं मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम् ॥
2.45.m: And through subsequent rites, there is no [further worldly] destination for him. / All this was spoken by Brahmā to the sages whose minds were purified.

2.45.s:
punaḥ sanatkumārāya kathitaṃ tena dhīmatā /
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanāyaiva kathitaṃ brahmasūnunā //
2.45.d:
पुनः सनत्कुमाराय कथितं तेन धीमता ।
कृष्णद्वैपायनायैव कथितं ब्रह्मसूनुना ॥
2.45.m: Again it was told to Sanatkumāra by that wise one; / by the son of Brahmā it was told to Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

2.45.s:
prasādāttasya devasya vedavyāsasya dhīmataḥ /
jñātaṃ mayā kṛtaṃ caiva niyogādeva tasya tu //
2.45.d:
प्रसादात्तस्य देवस्य वेदव्यासस्य धीमतः ।
ज्ञातं मया कृतं चैव नियोगादेव तस्य तु ॥
2.45.m: By the grace of that divine, wise Veda Vyāsa, / it was understood by me and performed by me by his command alone.

2.45.s:
etadvaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ rahasyaṃ brahmasiddhidam /
muniputrāya dātavyaṃ na cābhaktāya suvratāḥ //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge jīvacchrādvavidhirnāma pañcacatvāriṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.45.d:
एतद्वः कथितं सर्वं रहस्यं ब्रह्मसिद्धिदम् ।
मुनिपुत्राय दातव्यं न चाभक्ताय सुव्रताः ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे जीवच्छ्राद्वविधिर्नाम पञ्चचत्वारिंशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.45.m:
All this secret granting the attainment of Brahman has been told to you; / it should be given to a sage's son and not to an unbeliever, O you of noble vows."

Thus ends the forty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Procedure of Śrāddha Performed While Living', in the second part of the glorious Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

2.46.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
jīvacchrāddhavidhiḥ proktastvayā sūta mahāmate /
mṛrkhāṇāmapi mokṣārthamasmākaṃ romaharṣaṇa //
2.46.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
जीवच्छ्राद्धविधिः प्रोक्तस्त्वया सूत महामते ।
मृर्खाणामपि मोक्षार्थमस्माकं रोमहर्षण ॥
2.46.m: The sages said: / "The procedure of śrāddha while living was spoken by you, O wise Sūta, / for the liberation of even the ignorant among us, O Romaharṣaṇa.

2.46.s:
rudrādityavasūnāṃ ca śakraādīnāṃ ca suvrata /
pratiṣṭhā kīdṛśī śaṃbhorligamūrteśca śobhanā //
2.46.d:
रुद्रादित्यवसूनां च शक्रआदीनां च सुव्रत ।
प्रतिष्ठा कीदृशी शंभोर्लिगमूर्तेश्च शोभना ॥
2.46.m: What kind is the auspicious installation of the Rudras, Ādityas, Vasus, / and Indra and the others, O you of noble vows, and of Śaṃbhu whose form is the liṅga?

2.46.s:
viṣṇoḥ śakrasya devasya brahmaṇaśca mahātmanaḥ /
agner yasya nirṛter varuṇasya mahādyuteḥ //
2.46.d:
विष्णोः शक्रस्य देवस्य ब्रह्मणश्च महात्मनः ।
अग्नेर् यस्य निरृतेर् वरुणस्य महाद्युतेः ॥
2.46.m: [What is the installation] of Viṣṇu, the god Indra, and the great-souled Brahmā, / of Agni, of Yama, of Nirṛti, and of Varuṇa of great splendour,

2.46.s:
vāyoḥ somasya yakṣasya kuberasyāmitātmanaḥ /
īśānasya dharāyāśca śrīpratiṣṭhātha vā katham //
2.46.d:
वायोः सोमस्य यक्षस्य कुबेरस्यामितात्मनः ।
ईशानस्य धरायाश्च श्रीप्रतिष्ठाथ वा कथम् ॥
2.46.m: of Vāyu, of Soma, of the yakṣa Kubera of boundless soul, / of Īśāna and of Dharā, or how is the installation of Śrī?

2.46.s:
durgāśivāpratiṣṭhā ca haimavatyāśca śobhanā /
skandasya gaṇarājasya nandinaśca viśeṣataḥ //
2.46.d:
दुर्गाशिवाप्रतिष्ठा च हैमवत्याश्च शोभना ।
स्कन्दस्य गणराजस्य नन्दिनश्च विशेषतः ॥
2.46.m: And the auspicious installation of Durgā, Śivā, and Haimavatī, / and especially of Skanda, of Gaṇarāja, and of Nandin,

2.46.s:
tathānyeṣāṃ ca devānāṃ gaṇānāmapi vā punaḥ /
pratiṣṭhālakṣaṇaṃ sarvaṃ vistāradvaktumarhasi //
2.46.d:
तथान्येषां च देवानां गणानामपि वा पुनः ।
प्रतिष्ठालक्षणं सर्वं विस्तारद्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.46.m: and also of the other gods, or moreover of the gaṇas— / you ought to tell the entire character of installation at length.

2.46.s:
bhavānsarvārthatattvajño rudrabhaktaśca suvrata /
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasyāsi sākṣāttvamaparā tanuḥ //
2.46.d:
भवान्सर्वार्थतत्त्वज्ञो रुद्रभक्तश्च सुव्रत ।
कृष्णद्वैपायनस्यासि साक्षात्त्वमपरा तनुः ॥
2.46.m: You know the true reality of all matters, and you are devoted to Rudra, O you of noble vows; / you are visibly a second body of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

2.46.s:
sumanturjaiminiścaiva pailaśca paramarṣayaḥ /
gurubhaktiṃ tathā kartuṃ samartho romaharṣaṇaḥ //
2.46.d:
सुमन्तुर्जैमिनिश्चैव पैलश्च परमर्षयः ।
गुरुभक्तिं तथा कर्तुं समर्थो रोमहर्षणः ॥
2.46.m: Sumantu, Jaimini, and Paila are supreme sages, / [yet] Romaharṣaṇa is [most] capable of rendering devotion to the guru.

2.46.s:
iti vyāsasya vipulā gāthā bhāgīrathītaṭe /
ekaḥ samo vā bhinno vā śiṣyastasya mahādyuteḥ //
2.46.d:
इति व्यासस्य विपुला गाथा भागीरथीतटे ।
एकः समो वा भिन्नो वा शिष्यस्तस्य महाद्युतेः ॥
2.46.m: Thus was the vast praise of Vyāsa on the bank of the Bhāgīrathī: / that the disciple of that one of great splendour is unique, whether equal or different.

2.46.s:
vaiśaṃpāyanatulyo 'si vyāsaśiṣyeṣu bhūtale /
tasmādasmākamakhilaṃ vaktumarhasi sāṃpratam //
2.46.d:
वैशंपायनतुल्यो ऽसि व्यासशिष्येषु भूतले ।
तस्मादस्माकमखिलं वक्तुमर्हसि सांप्रतम् ॥
2.46.m: You are equal to Vaiśaṃpāyana among the disciples of Vyāsa on earth; / therefore, you ought to tell all to us now."

2.46.s:
evamuktvā sthiteṣveva teṣu sarveṣu tatra ca /
babhūva vismayo 'tīva munīnāṃ tasya cāgrataḥ //
2.46.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स्थितेष्वेव तेषु सर्वेषु तत्र च ।
बभूव विस्मयो ऽतीव मुनीनां तस्य चाग्रतः ॥
2.46.m: When they had thus spoken and all remained there, / an exceedingly great wonder occurred before that sage.

2.46.s:
athāntarikṣe vipulā sākṣāddevī sarasvatī /
alaṃ munīnāṃ praśro 'yamiti vācā babhūva ha //
2.46.d:
अथान्तरिक्षे विपुला साक्षाद्देवी सरस्वती ।
अलं मुनीनां प्रश्रो ऽयमिति वाचा बभूव ह ॥
2.46.m: Then, in the sky, goddess Sarasvatī herself appeared in vast form / with a voice saying: "Enough of this inquiry of the sages!

2.46.s:
sarvaṃ liṅgamayaṃ lokaṃ sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam /
tasmātsarvaṃ parityajya sthāpayetpūjayecca tat //
2.46.d:
सर्वं लिङ्गमयं लोकं सर्वं लिङ्गे प्रतिष्ठितम् ।
तस्मात्सर्वं परित्यज्य स्थापयेत्पूजयेच्च तत् ॥
2.46.m: The entire world consists of the liṅga; everything is established in the liṅga; / therefore, abandoning everything, one should install and worship it.

2.46.s:
liṅgasthāpanasanmārganihitasvāyatāsinā /
āśu brahmāṇḍamudbhidya nirgacchedaviśaṅkayā //
2.46.d:
लिङ्गस्थापनसन्मार्गनिहितस्वायतासिना ।
आशु ब्रह्माण्डमुद्भिद्य निर्गच्छेदविशङ्कया ॥
2.46.m: With the long sword of one's own control placed in the noble path of installing the liṅga, / one quickly pierces the cosmic egg and emerges without doubt.

2.46.s:
upedrāṃbhojagarbhendrayamāṃbudhanadeśvarāḥ /
tathānye ca śivaṃ sthāpya liṅgamūrti maheśvaram //
2.46.d:
उपेद्रांभोजगर्भेन्द्रयमांबुधनदेश्वराः ।
तथान्ये च शिवं स्थाप्य लिङ्गमूर्ति महेश्वरम् ॥
2.46.m: Upendra, the lotus-born [Brahmā], Indra, Yama, the lord of waters [Varuṇa], the lord of wealth [Kubera], / and others, having installed Śiva, Maheśvara whose form is the liṅga,

2.46.s:
sveṣusveṣu ca pakṣeṣu pradhānāste yathā dvijāḥ /
brahmā haraśca bhagavānviṣṇurdevī ramā dharā //
2.46.d:
स्वेषुस्वेषु च पक्षेषु प्रधानास्ते यथा द्विजाः ।
ब्रह्मा हरश्च भगवान्विष्णुर्देवी रमा धरा ॥
2.46.m: became foremost in their respective domains, O twice-born ones: / Brahmā, the Lord Hara, Viṣṇu, the goddess Ramā, Dharā,

2.46.s:
lakṣmīrdhṛtiḥ smṛtiḥ prajñā dharā durgā śacī tathā /
rudrāśca vasavaḥ skando viśākhaḥ śākha eva ca //
2.46.d:
लक्ष्मीर्धृतिः स्मृतिः प्रज्ञा धरा दुर्गा शची तथा ।
रुद्राश्च वसवः स्कन्दो विशाखः शाख एव च ॥
2.46.m: Lakṣmī, Dhṛti, Smṛti, Prajñā, Dharā, Durgā, and Śacī, / and the Rudras, the Vasus, Skanda, Viśākha, and Śākha,

2.46.s:
naigameśaśca bhagavāṃllokapālā grahāstathā /
sarve nandipurogāśca gaṇā gaṇapatiḥ prabhuḥ //
2.46.d:
नैगमेशश्च भगवांल्लोकपाला ग्रहास्तथा ।
सर्वे नन्दिपुरोगाश्च गणा गणपतिः प्रभुः ॥
2.46.m: and the divine Naigameśa, the world guardians (lokapālas), and the planets, / all the gaṇas led by Nandin, the lord Gaṇapati,

2.46.s:
pitaro munayaḥ sarve kuberādyāśca suprabhāḥ /
āditya vasavaḥ sāṃkhyā aśvinau ca bhiṣagvarau //
2.46.d:
पितरो मुनयः सर्वे कुबेराद्याश्च सुप्रभाः ।
आदित्य वसवः सांख्या अश्विनौ च भिषग्वरौ ॥
2.46.m: all the ancestors, the sages, Kubera and others of great lustre, / the Ādityas, the Vasus, the Sāṃkhyas, and the Aśvins, the best of physicians."

2.46.s:
viśvedevāśca sādhyāśca paśavaḥ pakṣiṇo mṛgāḥ /
brahmādisthāvarāntaṃ ca sarvaṃ liṅge pratiṣṭhitam //
2.46.d:
विश्वेदेवाश्च साध्याश्च पशवः पक्षिणो मृगाः ।
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तं च सर्वं लिङ्गे प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
2.46.m:
and the Viśvedevas, the Sādhyas, beasts, birds, and game animals,
and all things from Brahmā down to immovable objects, are established in the liṅga.

2.46.s:
tasmātsarvaṃ parityajya sthāpayelliṅgamavyayam /
yatnena stāpitaṃ sarvaṃ pūjitaṃ pūjayedyadi //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.46.d:
तस्मात्सर्वं परित्यज्य स्थापयेल्लिङ्गमव्ययम् ।
यत्नेन स्तापितं सर्वं पूजितं पूजयेद्यदि ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे षट्चत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः

2.47.s:
sūta uvāca
iti niśamya kṛtāñjalaya stadā divi mahāmunayaḥ kṛtaniścayāḥ /
śivataraṃ śivamīśvaramavyayaṃ manasi liṅgamayaṃ praṇipatya te //
2.47.d:
सूत उवाच
इति निशम्य कृताञ्जलय स्तदा दिवि महामुनयः कृतनिश्चयाः ।
शिवतरं शिवमीश्वरमव्ययं मनसि लिङ्गमयं प्रणिपत्य ते ॥
2.47.m:
Sūta said:
Having heard this, the great sages, standing with folded hands in the sky and firm in their resolve,
having bowed down in their minds to the most auspicious Śiva, the imperishable Lord, who consists of the liṅga,

2.47.s:
sakaladevapatirbhagavānajo hariraśeṣapatirguruṇā svayam /
munivarāśca gaṇāśca surāsurā naravarāḥ śivaliṅgamayāḥ punaḥ //
2.47.d:
सकलदेवपतिर्भगवानजो हरिरशेषपतिर्गुरुणा स्वयम् ।
मुनिवराश्च गणाश्च सुरासुरा नरवराः शिवलिङ्गमयाः पुनः ॥
2.47.m:
the venerable unborn Lord of all gods, Hari the Lord of all, and the Guru himself,
and the eminent sages, the gaṇas, the gods and asuras, and the best of men, who are in turn composed of the liṅga of Śiva,

2.47.s:
śrutvaivaṃ munayaḥ sarve ṣaṭkulīyāḥ samāhitāḥ /
saṃtyajya sarvaṃ devasya pratiṣṭhāṃ kartumudyatāḥ //
2.47.d:
श्रुत्वैवं मुनयः सर्वे षट्कुलीयाः समाहिताः ।
संत्यज्य सर्वं देवस्य प्रतिष्ठां कर्तुमुद्यताः ॥
2.47.m:
Having thus heard, all the concentrated sages belonging to the six lineages,
renouncing everything, undertook to perform the installation of the Lord.

2.47.s:
apṛcchansūtamanaghaṃ harṣagadgadayā girā /
liṅgapratiṣṭhāṃ vipulāṃ sarve te śaṃsitavratāḥ //
2.47.d:
अपृच्छन्सूतमनघं हर्षगद्गदया गिरा ।
लिङ्गप्रतिष्ठां विपुलां सर्वे ते शंसितव्रताः ॥
2.47.m:
All those who were praised for their vows asked the sinless Sūta,
with voices faltering with joy, about the extensive installation of the liṅga:

2.47.s:
sūta uvāca
pratiṣṭhāṃ liṅgamūrtervo yathāvadanupūrvaśaḥ /
pravakṣyāmi samāsena dharmakāmārthamuktaye //
2.47.d:
सूत उवाच
प्रतिष्ठां लिङ्गमूर्तेर्वो यथावदनुपूर्वशः ।
प्रवक्ष्यामि समासेन धर्मकामार्थमुक्तये ॥
2.47.m:
Sūta said:
I shall explain to you concisely the installation of the liṅga-form, in proper order
and according to rule, for the sake of dharma, desire, wealth, and liberation.

2.47.s:
kṛtvaiva liṅgaṃ vidhinā bhuvi liṅgeṣu yatnataḥ /
liṅgamekatamaṃ śailaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivātmakam //
2.47.d:
कृत्वैव लिङ्गं विधिना भुवि लिङ्गेषु यत्नतः ।
लिङ्गमेकतमं शैलं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवात्मकम् ॥
2.47.m:
Having made a liṅga according to rule among the liṅgas on earth with care,
any single liṅga made of stone, embodying Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,

2.47.s:
hemaratnamayaṃ vāpi rājataṃ tāmrajaṃ tu vā /
savedikaṃ sasūtraṃ ca samyagvistṛtamastakam //
2.47.d:
हेमरत्नमयं वापि राजतं ताम्रजं तु वा ।
सवेदिकं ससूत्रं च सम्यग्विस्तृतमस्तकम् ॥
2.47.m:
or one made of gold, gems, silver, or copper,
furnished with a pedestal, with the thread, and with a fully widened top,

2.47.s:
viśodhya sthāpayedbhaktyā savedikamanuttamam /
liṅgavedī umā devī liṅgaṃ sākṣānmaheśvaraḥ //
2.47.d:
विशोध्य स्थापयेद्भक्त्या सवेदिकमनुत्तमम् ।
लिङ्गवेदी उमा देवी लिङ्गं साक्षान्महेश्वरः ॥
2.47.m:
having purified it, one should install with devotion that unexcelled [liṅga] along with its pedestal;
the pedestal of the liṅga is the goddess Umā, and the liṅga is Maheśvara himself.

2.47.s:
tayoḥ sapūjanādeva devī devaśca pūjitau /
pratiṣṭhayā ca deveśo devyā sārdhaṃ pratiṣṭhitaḥ //
2.47.d:
तयोः सपूजनादेव देवी देवश्च पूजितौ ।
प्रतिष्ठया च देवेशो देव्या सार्धं प्रतिष्ठितः ॥
2.47.m:
By the worship of them both, the Goddess and the God are worshipped,
and by its installation, the Lord of Gods is installed together with the Goddess.

2.47.s: tasmātsavedikaṃ liṅgaṃ sthāpayetsthāpakottamaḥ //
2.47.d: तस्मात्सवेदिकं लिङ्गं स्थापयेत्स्थापकोत्तमः ॥
2.47.m: Therefore, the best of installers should install the liṅga along with its pedestal.

2.47.s:
mūle brahmā vasati bhagavānmadhyabhāge ca viṣṇuḥ sarveśānaḥ /
paśupatirajo rudramūrtirvareṇyaḥ /
tasmālliṅgaṃ gurutarataraṃ pūjayetsthāpayedvā yasmātpūjyo gaṇapatirasau devamukhyaiḥ samastaiḥ //
2.47.d:
मूले ब्रह्मा वसति भगवान्मध्यभागे च विष्णुः सर्वेशानः ।
पशुपतिरजो रुद्रमूर्तिर्वरेण्यः ।
तस्माल्लिङ्गं गुरुतरतरं पूजयेत्स्थापयेद्वा यस्मात्पूज्यो गणपतिरसौ देवमुख्यैः समस्तैः ॥
2.47.m:
The venerable Brahmā dwells at the base, Viṣṇu in the middle, and the unborn Paśupati, the lord of all, the desirable one in the form of Rudra, [at the top];
therefore, one should worship or install the liṅga as weightier than the weightiest, because this lord of gaṇas is worshipped by all the foremost gods.

2.47.s:
gandhaiḥ sragdhūpadīpaiḥ snapanahutabalistotramantropahārairnityaṃ ye 'bhyarcayānti tridaśavaratanuṃ liṅgamūrtiṃ maheśam /
garbhādhānādināśakṣayabhayarahitā devagandharvamukhyaiḥ siddhairvandyāśca pūjyā gaṇavaranamitāste bhavantyaprameyāḥ //
2.47.d:
गन्धैः स्रग्धूपदीपैः स्नपनहुतबलिस्तोत्रमन्त्रोपहारैर्नित्यं ये ऽभ्यर्चयान्ति त्रिदशवरतनुं लिङ्गमूर्तिं महेशम् ।
गर्भाधानादिनाशक्षयभयरहिता देवगन्धर्वमुख्यैः सिद्धैर्वन्द्याश्च पूज्या गणवरनमितास्ते भवन्त्यप्रमेयाः ॥
2.47.m:
Those who constantly worship Maheśa in the form of the liṅga, whose body is the best among the thirty [gods], with perfumes, garlands, incense, lamps, ablutions, oblations, bali-offerings, hymns of praise, and offerings of mantras,
become free from the fear of birth, destruction, and decay; worthy of adoration and praise by the chiefs of the gods and gandharvas and by the siddhas, bowed to by the best of the gaṇas, they become immeasurable.

2.47.s:
tasmādbhaktyopacāreṇa sthāpayetparameśvaram /
pūjayecca viśeṣeṇa liṅgaṃ sarvārthasiddhaye //
2.47.d:
तस्माद्भक्त्योपचारेण स्थापयेत्परमेश्वरम् ।
पूजयेच्च विशेषेण लिङ्गं सर्वार्थसिद्धये ॥
2.47.m:
Therefore, one should install the Supreme Lord with devotion and proper ritual services,
and especially worship the liṅga for the attainment of all ends.

2.47.s:
samarcya sthāpayelliṅgaṃ tīrthamadhye śivāsane /
kūrcavastrādibhirliṅgamācchādya kalaśaiḥ punaḥ //
2.47.d:
समर्च्य स्थापयेल्लिङ्गं तीर्थमध्ये शिवासने ।
कूर्चवस्त्रादिभिर्लिङ्गमाच्छाद्य कलशैः पुनः ॥
2.47.m:
Having worshipped [it], one should place the liṅga in a sacred place on a seat of Śiva,
covering the liṅga with kūrcas, cloths, and the like, and then with water-jars,

2.47.s:
lokapālādidaivatyaiḥ sakūrcaiḥ sākṣataiḥ śubhaiḥ /
utkūrcaiḥ svastikādyaiśca citratantukaveṣṭitaiḥ //
2.47.d:
लोकपालादिदैवत्यैः सकूर्चैः साक्षतैः शुभैः ।
उत्कूर्चैः स्वस्तिकाद्यैश्च चित्रतन्तुकवेष्टितैः ॥
2.47.m:
which have deities beginning with the world-protectors, accompanied by kūrcas, unbroken grains, auspicious,
with elevated kūrcas, svastikas and the like, wrapped with variegated threads,

2.47.s:
vajrādikāyudopetaiḥ savastraiḥ sapidhānakaiḥ /
lakṣayetparito liṅgamīśānena pratiṣṭhitam //
2.47.d:
वज्रादिकायुदोपेतैः सवस्त्रैः सपिधानकैः ।
लक्षयेत्परितो लिङ्गमीशानेन प्रतिष्ठितम् ॥
2.47.m:
equipped with weapons beginning with the vajra, with cloths, and with lids;
one should mark the installed liṅga all around by means of Īśāna,

2.47.s:
dhūpadīpasamopetaṃ vitānavitatāṃbaram /
lokapāladhvajaiścaiva gajādimahiṣādibhiḥ //
2.47.d:
धूपदीपसमोपेतं वितानविततांबरम् ।
लोकपालध्वजैश्चैव गजादिमहिषादिभिः ॥
2.47.m:
provided with incense and lamps, with a canopy of stretched cloth,
and with banners of the world-protectors [bearing] elephants, buffaloes, and the like,

2.47.s:
citritaiḥ pūjitaiścaiva darbhamālā ca śobhanā /
sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpūrṇā tayā bāhye ca veṣṭayet //
2.47.d:
चित्रितैः पूजितैश्चैव दर्भमाला च शोभना ।
सर्वलक्षणसंपूर्णा तया बाह्ये च वेष्टयेत् ॥
2.47.m:
adorned and worshipped; and with an auspicious garland of darbha grass,
complete with all auspicious marks, one should encircle it on the outside.

2.47.s:
tatodhivāsayettoye dhūpadīpasamanvite /
pañcāhaṃ vā tryahaṃvātha ekarātramadhāpi vā //
2.47.d:
ततोधिवासयेत्तोये धूपदीपसमन्विते ।
पञ्चाहं वा त्र्यहंवाथ एकरात्रमधापि वा ॥
2.47.m:
Then one should keep it immersed in water accompanied by incense and lamps,
for five days, three days, or even for a single night,

2.47.s:
vedādhyayanasaṃpanno nṛtyagītādimaṅgalaiḥ /
kiṅkiṇīravakopetaṃ tālavīṇāravairapi //
2.47.d:
वेदाध्ययनसंपन्नो नृत्यगीतादिमङ्गलैः ।
किङ्किणीरवकोपेतं तालवीणारवैरपि ॥
2.47.m:
rich in the recitation of the Vedas, with auspicious celebrations like dance and song,
accompanied by the tinkling of small bells, and also by the sounds of cymbals and lutes.

2.47.s:
īkṣayetkālamavyagro yajamānaḥ samāhitaḥ /
utthāpya svastikaṃ dhyāyenmaṇḍape lakṣaṇānvite //
2.47.d:
ईक्षयेत्कालमव्यग्रो यजमानः समाहितः ।
उत्थाप्य स्वस्तिकं ध्यायेन्मण्डपे लक्षणान्विते ॥
2.47.m:
The patron of the sacrifice, attentive and composed, should watch the time;
having raised [the liṅga], one should meditate on the svastika in a pavilion endowed with the proper characteristics,

2.47.s:
saṃskṛte vedisaṃyukte navakuṇḍena saṃvṛte /
pūrvokta vidhinā yukte sarvalakṣaṇasaṃyute //
2.47.d:
संस्कृते वेदिसंयुक्ते नवकुण्डेन संवृते ।
पूर्वोक्त विधिना युक्ते सर्वलक्षणसंयुते ॥
2.47.m:
consecrated, furnished with a pedestal, surrounded by nine fire-pits,
accompanied by the previously stated procedure, possessed of all characteristic marks,

2.47.s:
aṣṭamaṇḍalasaṃyukte digdhvajāṣṭakasaṃyute /
pūrvoktalakṣaṇopetaiḥ kuṇḍaiḥ prāgāditaḥ kramāt //
2.47.d:
अष्टमण्डलसंयुक्ते दिग्ध्वजाष्टकसंयुते ।
पूर्वोक्तलक्षणोपेतैः कुण्डैः प्रागादितः क्रमात् ॥
2.47.m:
furnished with eight maṇḍalas, equipped with the eight banners of the directions,
with fire-pits endowed with the previously stated characteristics, in order beginning from the east.

2.47.s:
pradhānaṃ kuṇḍamīśānyāṃ caturasraṃ vidhīyate /
athavā pañcakuṇḍaikaṃ sthaṇḍilaṃ caikameva ca //
2.47.d:
प्रधानं कुण्डमीशान्यां चतुरस्रं विधीयते ।
अथवा पञ्चकुण्डैकं स्थण्डिलं चैकमेव च ॥
2.47.m:
The principal fire-pit in the north-east is prescribed to be square;
or else five fire-pits and one elevated ground [for oblations] are to be made.

2.47.s:
yajñopakaraṇaiḥ sarvaiḥ śivārcāyāṃ hi bhūṣaṇaiḥ /
vedimadhye mahāśayyāṃ pañcatūlīprakalpitām //
2.47.d:
यज्ञोपकरणैः सर्वैः शिवार्चायां हि भूषणैः ।
वेदिमध्ये महाशय्यां पञ्चतूलीप्रकल्पिताम् ॥
2.47.m:
With all the implements of the sacrifice and with ornaments for the worship of Śiva,
[one should arrange] a great bed prepared with five layers of cotton in the middle of the altar;

2.47.s:
kalpayetkāñcanopetāṃ sitavastrāvaguṇṭhitām /
prakalpyaivaṃ śivaṃ caiva sthāpayetparameśvaram //
2.47.d:
कल्पयेत्काञ्चनोपेतां सितवस्त्रावगुण्ठिताम् ।
प्रकल्प्यैवं शिवं चैव स्थापयेत्परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.47.m:
one should prepare [the bed] furnished with gold and covered with white cloth;
having thus prepared it, one should lay down Śiva, the Supreme Lord.

2.47.s:
prākśiraskaṃ nyaselliṅgamīśānena yathāvidhi /
ratnanyāse kṛte pūrva kevalaṃ kalaśaṃ nyaset //
2.47.d:
प्राक्शिरस्कं न्यसेल्लिङ्गमीशानेन यथाविधि ।
रत्नन्यासे कृते पूर्व केवलं कलशं न्यसेत् ॥
2.47.m:
One should place the liṅga with its head to the east according to the rule with the Īśāna [mantra];
when the deposit of gems has been performed earlier, one should place only the jar.

2.47.s:
liṅgamācchādya vastrābhyāṃ kūrcena ca samantataḥ /
ratnanyāse prasakte 'tha vāmādyā nava śaktayaḥ //
2.47.d:
लिङ्गमाच्छाद्य वस्त्राभ्यां कूर्चेन च समन्ततः ।
रत्नन्यासे प्रसक्ते ऽथ वामाद्या नव शक्तयः ॥
2.47.m:
Having covered the liṅga with two cloths and with a kūrca on all sides,
when the deposit of gems is commenced, then the nine powers beginning with Vāmā,

2.47.s:
navaratnaṃ hiraṇyādyaiḥ pañcagavyena saṃyutaiḥ /
sarvadānyasamopetaṃ śilāyāmapi vinyaset //
2.47.d:
नवरत्नं हिरण्याद्यैः पञ्चगव्येन संयुतैः ।
सर्वदान्यसमोपेतं शिलायामपि विन्यसेत् ॥
2.47.m:
the nine gems, along with gold and the like, together with the five products of the cow,
and accompanied by all kinds of grains, one should deposit even upon the stone.

2.47.s:
sthāpayedbrahmaliṅgaṃ hi śivagāyatrisaṃyutam /
kevalaṃ praṇavenāpi sthāpayecchivamavyayam //
2.47.d:
स्थापयेद्ब्रह्मलिङ्गं हि शिवगायत्रिसंयुतम् ।
केवलं प्रणवेनापि स्थापयेच्छिवमव्ययम् ॥
2.47.m:
One should indeed install the liṅga of Brahman accompanied by the Śivagāyatrī,
or one may install the imperishable Śiva with the praṇava alone.

2.47.s:
brahmajajñānamantreṇa brahmabhāgaṃ prabhostathā /
viṣṇugāyatriyā bhāgaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tvatha vinyaset //
2.47.d:
ब्रह्मजज्ञानमन्त्रेण ब्रह्मभागं प्रभोस्तथा ।
विष्णुगायत्रिया भागं वैष्णवं त्वथ विन्यसेत् ॥
2.47.m:
With the brahmajajñāna mantra one should deposit the portion of the Lord belonging to Brahmā,
and with the Viṣṇugāyatrī one should deposit the portion belonging to Viṣṇu.

2.47.s:
sūtre tattvatrayopete praṇavena pravinyaset /
sarvaṃ namaḥ śivāyeti namo haṃsaḥ śivāya ca //
2.47.d:
सूत्रे तत्त्वत्रयोपेते प्रणवेन प्रविन्यसेत् ।
सर्वं नमः शिवायेति नमो हंसः शिवाय च ॥
2.47.m:
Upon the thread endowed with the three principles one should deposit with the praṇava,
and everything with 'namaḥ śivāya' and 'namo haṃsaḥ śivāya'.

2.47.s:
rudrādhyāyena vā sarvaṃ parimṛjya ca vinyaset /
sthāpayedbrahmabhiścaiva kalaśānvai samantataḥ //
2.47.d:
रुद्राध्यायेन वा सर्वं परिमृज्य च विन्यसेत् ।
स्थापयेद्ब्रह्मभिश्चैव कलशान्वै समन्ततः ॥
2.47.m:
Or, having wiped everything, one should deposit it with the Rudrādhyāya,
and with the brahma-mantras one should install the jars on all sides.

2.47.s:
vedimadhye nyasetsarvānmūrvoktavidhisaṃyutān /
madhyakuṃbhe śivaṃ devīṃ dakṣiṇe parameśvarīm //
2.47.d:
वेदिमध्ये न्यसेत्सर्वान्मूर्वोक्तविधिसंयुतान् ।
मध्यकुंभे शिवं देवीं दक्षिणे परमेश्वरीम् ॥
2.47.m:
In the middle of the altar one should place all of them endowed with the previously stated rule;
in the central jar [one should invoke] Śiva, and in the southern [jar] the goddess, the Supreme Mistress;

2.47.s:
skandaṃ tayośca madhye tu skandakuṃbhe sucitrite /
brahmāṇaṃ skandakuṃbhe vā īśakumbhe hariṃ tathā //
2.47.d:
स्कन्दं तयोश्च मध्ये तु स्कन्दकुंभे सुचित्रिते ।
ब्रह्माणं स्कन्दकुंभे वा ईशकुम्भे हरिं तथा ॥
2.47.m:
and between the two, Skanda in the well-decorated jar of Skanda;
or Brahmā in the jar of Skanda, and likewise Hari in the jar of Īśa;

2.47.s:
athavā śivakuṃbhe ca brahmāṅgāni ca vinyaset /
śivo maheśvaraścaiva rudro viṣṇuḥ pitāmahaḥ //
2.47.d:
अथवा शिवकुंभे च ब्रह्माङ्गानि च विन्यसेत् ।
शिवो महेश्वरश्चैव रुद्रो विष्णुः पितामहः ॥
2.47.m:
or in the jar of Śiva one should deposit the brahmāṅgas:
Śiva, Maheśvara, Rudra, Viṣṇu, and Pitāmaha;

2.47.s:
brahmāṇyevaṃ samāsena hṛdayādīni cāṃbikā /
vedimadhye nyasetsarvānpūrvoktavidhisaṃyutān //
2.47.d:
ब्रह्माण्येवं समासेन हृदयादीनि चांबिका ।
वेदिमध्ये न्यसेत्सर्वान्पूर्वोक्तविधिसंयुतान् ॥
2.47.m:
thus briefly the brahmāṅgas, the heart and so forth, and Ambikā;
in the middle of the altar one should place all of them endowed with the previously stated rule.

2.47.s:
vardhanyāṃ sthāpayeddevīṃ gandhatoyena pūrya ca /
hiraṇyaṃ rajataṃ ratnaṃ śivakuṃbhe pravinyaset //
2.47.d:
वर्धन्यां स्थापयेद्देवीं गन्धतोयेन पूर्य च ।
हिरण्यं रजतं रत्नं शिवकुंभे प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
2.47.m:
One should establish the Goddess in the vardhanī vessel, having filled it with perfumed water;
gold, silver, and jewels one should place in the jar of Śiva.

2.47.s:
vardhanyāmāpi yatnena gāyatryaṅgaiśca suvratāḥ /
vidyeśvarāndiśaṃ kuṃbhe brahmakūrcena pūrite //
2.47.d:
वर्धन्यामापि यत्नेन गायत्र्यङ्गैश्च सुव्रताः ।
विद्येश्वरान्दिशं कुंभे ब्रह्मकूर्चेन पूरिते ॥
2.47.m:
O you of good vows, [one should deposit jewels] in the vardhanī vessel also with care, and with the limbs of the Gāyatrī;
[and establish] the Vidyeśvaras in the jars of the directions filled with brahmakūrca,

2.47.s:
aṃnateśādidevāṃśca praṇavādinamontakam /
navavastraṃ pratighaṭamaṣṭakuṃbheṣu dāpayet //
2.47.d:
अंनतेशादिदेवांश्च प्रणवादिनमोन्तकम् ।
नववस्त्रं प्रतिघटमष्टकुंभेषु दापयेत् ॥
2.47.m:
and the deities beginning with Ananteśa, using [mantras] beginning with the praṇava and ending with 'namaḥ';
one should offer a new cloth to each pot, on the eight jars.

2.47.s:
vidyeśvarāṇāṃ kuṃbheṣu hemaratnādi vinyaset /
vaktrakrameṇa hotavyaṃ gāyatryaṅgakrameṇa ca //
2.47.d:
विद्येश्वराणां कुंभेषु हेमरत्नादि विन्यसेत् ।
वक्त्रक्रमेण होतव्यं गायत्र्यङ्गक्रमेण च ॥
2.47.m:
In the jars of the Vidyeśvaras one should place gold, gems, and the like;
one should offer oblations in the order of the faces [of Śiva] and in the order of the limbs of the Gāyatrī.

2.47.s:
jayādisviṣṭaparyantaṃ sarvaṃ pūrvavadācaret /
secayecchivakuṃbhena vardhanyā vaiṣṇavena ca //
2.47.d:
जयादिस्विष्टपर्यन्तं सर्वं पूर्ववदाचरेत् ।
सेचयेच्छिवकुंभेन वर्धन्या वैष्णवेन च ॥
2.47.m:
From the jaya offerings up to the sviṣṭakṛt, one should perform everything as before;
one should sprinkle [the liṅga] with the jar of Śiva, with the vardhanī, and with the [jar] of Viṣṇu.

2.47.s:
paitā mahena kuṃbhena brahmabhāgaṃ viśeṣataḥ /
vidyeśvarāṇāṃ kuṃbhaiśca secayetparameśvaram //
2.47.d:
पैता महेन कुंभेन ब्रह्मभागं विशेषतः ।
विद्येश्वराणां कुंभैश्च सेचयेत्परमेश्वरम् ॥
2.47.m: With the pitcher belonging to Pitāmaha [he should bathe] the Brahmā portion in particular, / and with the pitchers of the Vidyeśvaras he should bathe the Supreme Lord.

2.47.s:
vinyasetsarvamantrāṇi pūrvavatsusamāhitaḥ /
pūjayetsnapanaṃ kṛtvā sahasrādiṣu saṃbhavaiḥ //
2.47.d:
विन्यसेत्सर्वमन्त्राणि पूर्ववत्सुसमाहितः ।
पूजयेत्स्नपनं कृत्वा सहस्रादिषु संभवैः ॥
2.47.m: Well-composed, he should deposit all the mantras as before. / Having performed the ablution, he should worship with things produced from a thousand [cows] and so forth.

2.47.s:
dakṣiṇā ca pradātavyā sahasrapaṇamuttamam /
itareṣāṃ tadardhaṃ syāttadardhaṃ vā vidhīyate //
2.47.d:
दक्षिणा च प्रदातव्या सहस्रपणमुत्तमम् ।
इतरेषां तदर्धं स्यात्तदर्धं वा विधीयते ॥
2.47.m: And a priestly fee of an excellent thousand paṇas is to be given; / for the others, half of that or half of that [again] is prescribed.

2.47.s:
vastrāṇi ca pradhānasya kṣetrabhūṣaṇagodhanam /
utsavaśca prakartavyo homayagabaliḥ kramāt //
2.47.d:
वस्त्राणि च प्रधानस्य क्षेत्रभूषणगोधनम् ।
उत्सवश्च प्रकर्तव्यो होमयगबलिः क्रमात् ॥
2.47.m: And garments for the chief [priest], land, ornaments, and cattle. / And a festival is to be conducted, along with fire-offerings, sacrifices, and oblations in due course,

2.47.s:
navāhaṃ vāpi saptāhamekāhaṃ ca tryahaṃ tathā /
homaśca pūrvavatprokto nityamabhyarcya śaṅkaram //
2.47.d:
नवाहं वापि सप्ताहमेकाहं च त्र्यहं तथा ।
होमश्च पूर्ववत्प्रोक्तो नित्यमभ्यर्च्य शङ्करम् ॥
2.47.m: for nine days, or seven days, or one day, and likewise for three days. / And the fire-offering is declared as before, after worshipping Śaṅkara daily.

2.47.s:
devānāṃ bhāskarādīnāṃ homaṃ pūrvavadeva tu /
abhyantare tathā bāhye vahnau nityaṃ samarcayet //
2.47.d:
देवानां भास्करादीनां होमं पूर्ववदेव तु ।
अभ्यन्तरे तथा बाह्ये वह्नौ नित्यं समर्चयेत् ॥
2.47.m: The fire-offering for the deities beginning with the Sun is just as before; / he should constantly worship in the fire inside and outside.

2.47.s:
ya evaṃ sthāpayelliṅgaṃ sa eva parameśvaraḥ /
tena devagaṇā rudrā ṛṣayo 'psarasastathā //
2.47.d:
य एवं स्थापयेल्लिङ्गं स एव परमेश्वरः ।
तेन देवगणा रुद्रा ऋषयो ऽप्सरसस्तथा ॥
2.47.m: Whoever installs the liṅga in this manner is himself the Supreme Lord. / By him the hosts of gods, the Rudras, the sages, and likewise the apsarases

2.47.s:
sthāpitāḥ pūjitāścaiva trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge liṅgasthāpanaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.47.d:
स्थापिताः पूजिताश्चैव त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे लिङ्गस्थापनं नाम सप्तचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.47.m:
are installed and worshipped, and the three worlds with the moving and the unmoving.

Thus ends the forty-seventh chapter, entitled “Installation of the Liṅga,” in the second part of the glorious Liṅga Mahāpurāṇa.

2.48.s:
sūta uvāca
sarveṣāmapi devānāṃ pratiṣṭhāmapi vistarāt /
svairmatrairyāgakuṇḍāni vinyasyaikaikameva ca //
2.48.d:
सूत उवाच
सर्वेषामपि देवानां प्रतिष्ठामपि विस्तरात् ।
स्वैर्मत्रैर्यागकुण्डानि विन्यस्यैकैकमेव च ॥
2.48.m: Sūta said: / Now the installation of all the deities in detail: / laying out individual sacrificial fire-pits with their own mantras,

2.48.s:
sthāpayedutsavaṃ kṛtvā pūjayecca vidhānataḥ /
bhānoḥ pañcāgninā kāryaṃ dvādaśāgnikrameṇa vā //
2.48.d:
स्थापयेदुत्सवं कृत्वा पूजयेच्च विधानतः ।
भानोः पञ्चाग्निना कार्यं द्वादशाग्निक्रमेण वा ॥
2.48.m: he should install [each], conduct a festival, and worship according to rule. / For the Sun it is to be done with five fires, or by the sequence of twelve fires.

2.48.s:
sarvakuṇḍāni vṛttāni padmākārāṇi suvratāḥ /
aṃbāyā yonikuṇḍaṃ syādvardhanyekā vidhīyate //
2.48.d:
सर्वकुण्डानि वृत्तानि पद्माकाराणि सुव्रताः ।
अंबाया योनिकुण्डं स्याद्वर्धन्येका विधीयते ॥
2.48.m: All the pits are circular or lotus-shaped, O men of good vows. / For the Mother there should be a vulva-shaped pit, and one Vardhanī pitcher is prescribed.

2.48.s:
śaktīnāṃ sarvakāryeṣu yonikuṇḍaṃ vidhīyate /
gāyatrīṃ kalpayecchaṃbhoḥ sarveṣāmapi yatnataḥ /
sarve rudrāṃśajā yasmātsaṃkṣepeṇa vadāmi vaḥ //
2.48.d:
शक्तीनां सर्वकार्येषु योनिकुण्डं विधीयते ।
गायत्रीं कल्पयेच्छंभोः सर्वेषामपि यत्नतः ।
सर्वे रुद्रांशजा यस्मात्संक्षेपेण वदामि वः ॥
2.48.m: A vulva-shaped pit is prescribed in all rituals for the Śaktis. / One should carefully fashion Śambhu’s Gāyatrī for all of them; / since all are born from portions of Rudra, I shall tell you briefly.

2.48.s:
gāyatrībhedāḥ
tatpuruṣāya vidmahe vāgviśuddhāya dhīmahi /
tannaḥ śivaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
गायत्रीभेदाः
तत्पुरुषाय विद्महे वाग्विशुद्धाय धीमहि ।
तन्नः शिवः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: Varieties of the Gāyatrī: / “We know Tatpuruṣa; we meditate on the Purifier of Speech; / may Śiva inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
gaṇāṃbikāyai vidmahe karmasiddhyai ca dhīmahi /
tanno gaurī pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
गणांबिकायै विद्महे कर्मसिद्ध्यै च धीमहि ।
तन्नो गौरी प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Mother of the Hosts; we meditate on the Success of Action; / may Gaurī inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
tatpuruṣāya vidmahe mahādevāya dhīmahi /
tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
तत्पुरुषाय विद्महे महादेवाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो रुद्रः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know Tatpuruṣa; we meditate on Mahādeva; / may Rudra inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
tatpuruṣāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi /
tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
तत्पुरुषाय विद्महे वक्रतुण्डाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो दन्तिः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know Tatpuruṣa; we meditate on the Curved-Tusked One; / may the Tusked One inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
mahāsenāya vidmahe vāgviśuddhāya dhīmahi /
tannaḥ skandaḥ procadayāt //
2.48.d:
महासेनाय विद्महे वाग्विशुद्धाय धीमहि ।
तन्नः स्कन्दः प्रोचदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know Mahāsena; we meditate on the Purifier of Speech; / may Skanda inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
tīkṣṇaśṛṅgāya vidmahe vedapādāya dhīmahi /
tanno vṛṣaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
तीक्ष्णशृङ्गाय विद्महे वेदपादाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो वृषः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Sharp-Horned One; we meditate on the One whose Feet are the Vedas; / may the Bull inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
harivaktrāya vidmahe rudravaktrāya dhīmahi /
tanno nandī pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
हरिवक्त्राय विद्महे रुद्रवक्त्राय धीमहि ।
तन्नो नन्दी प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Lion-Faced One; we meditate on the Rudra-Faced One; / may Nandī inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
nārāyaṇāya vidmahe vāsudevāya dhīmahi /
tanno viṣṇuḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
नारायणाय विद्महे वासुदेवाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो विष्णुः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know Nārāyaṇa; we meditate on Vāsudeva; / may Viṣṇu inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
mahāṃbikāyai vidmahe karmasiddhaiya ca dhīmahi /
tanno lakṣmīḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
महांबिकायै विद्महे कर्मसिद्धैय च धीमहि ।
तन्नो लक्ष्मीः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Great Mother; we meditate on the Success of Action; / may Lakṣmī inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
samuddhṛtāyai vidmahe viṣṇunaikena dhīmahi /
tanno dharā pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
समुद्धृतायै विद्महे विष्णुनैकेन धीमहि ।
तन्नो धरा प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the One Lifted Up; we meditate on the One [lifted] by Viṣṇu alone; / may the Earth inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
vainateyāya vidmahe suvarṇapakṣāya dhīmahi /
tanno garuḍaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
वैनतेयाय विद्महे सुवर्णपक्षाय धीमहि ।
तन्नो गरुडः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Son of Vinatā; we meditate on the Golden-Winged One; / may Garuḍa inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
padmodbhavāya vidmahe vedavaktrāya dhīmahi /
tannaḥ sraṣṭā pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
पद्मोद्भवाय विद्महे वेदवक्त्राय धीमहि ।
तन्नः स्रष्टा प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Lotus-Born One; we meditate on the Veda-Mouthed One; / may the Creator inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
śivāsyajāyai vidmahe devarūpāyai dhīmahi /
tanno vācā pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
शिवास्यजायै विद्महे देवरूपायै धीमहि ।
तन्नो वाचा प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the One Born from Śiva’s Mouth; we meditate on the Divine-Formed One; / may Speech inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
devarājāya vidmahe vajrahastāya dhīmahi /
tannaḥ śakraḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
देवराजाय विद्महे वज्रहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नः शक्रः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the King of the Gods; we meditate on the Thunderbolt-in-Hand; / may Śakra inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
rudranetrāya vidmahe śaktihastāya dhīmahi /
tanno vahniḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
रुद्रनेत्राय विद्महे शक्तिहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो वह्निः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Eye of Rudra; we meditate on the Spear-in-Hand; / may Fire inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
vaivasvatāya vidmahe daṇḍahastāya dhīmahi /
tanno yamaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
वैवस्वताय विद्महे दण्डहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो यमः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Son of Vivasvat; we meditate on the Staff-in-Hand; / may Yama inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
niśācarāya vidmahe khaḍgahastāya dhīmahi /
tanno nirṛtiḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
निशाचराय विद्महे खड्गहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो निरृतिः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Night-Roamer; we meditate on the Sword-in-Hand; / may Nirṛti inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
śuddhahastāya vidmahe pāśahastāya dhīmahi /
tanno varuṇaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
शुद्धहस्ताय विद्महे पाशहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो वरुणः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Pure-Handed One; we meditate on the Noose-in-Hand; / may Varuṇa inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
sarpaprāṇāya vidmahe yaṣṭihastāya dhīmahi /
tanno vuyaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
सर्पप्राणाय विद्महे यष्टिहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो वुयः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Life-Breath of Serpents; we meditate on the Staff-in-Hand; / may Wind inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
yakṣeśvarāya vidmahe gadāhastāya dhīmahi /
tanno yakṣaḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
यक्षेश्वराय विद्महे गदाहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो यक्षः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Lord of the Yakṣas; we meditate on the Mace-in-Hand; / may the Yakṣa inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
sarveśvarāya vidmahe śūlahastāya dhīmahi /
tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
सर्वेश्वराय विद्महे शूलहस्ताय धीमहि ।
तन्नो रुद्रः प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know the Lord of All; we meditate on the Trident-in-Hand; / may Rudra inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
kātyāyanyai vidmahe kanyākumāryai dhīmahi /
tanno durgā pracodayāt //
2.48.d:
कात्यायन्यै विद्महे कन्याकुमार्यै धीमहि ।
तन्नो दुर्गा प्रचोदयात् ॥
2.48.m: “We know Kātyāyanī; we meditate on the Virgin Maiden; / may Durgā inspire us to that!”

2.48.s:
evaṃ prabhidya gāyatrīṃ tattadevānurūpataḥ /
pūjayet sthāpayetteṣāmāsanaṃ praṇavaṃ smṛtam //
2.48.d:
एवं प्रभिद्य गायत्रीं तत्तदेवानुरूपतः ।
पूजयेत् स्थापयेत्तेषामासनं प्रणवं स्मृतम् ॥
2.48.m: Having thus differentiated the Gāyatrī in accordance with each particular deity, / he should worship and install [them]; the Praṇava is traditionally handed down as their seat.

2.48.s:
athavā viṣṇumatulaṃ sūktena puruṣeṇa vā /
viṣṇuṃ caiva mahāviṣṇuṃ sadāviṣṇumanukramāt //
2.48.d:
अथवा विष्णुमतुलं सूक्तेन पुरुषेण वा ।
विष्णुं चैव महाविष्णुं सदाविष्णुमनुक्रमात् ॥
2.48.m: Alternatively, [he should install] the peerless Viṣṇu with the Puruṣa Sūkta, / and Viṣṇu, Mahāviṣṇu, and Sadāviṣṇu in order,

2.48.s:
sthāpayeddevagāyatryā parikalpya vidhānataḥ /
vāsudevaḥ pradhānastu tataḥ saṃkarṣaṇaḥ svayam //
2.48.d:
स्थापयेद्देवगायत्र्या परिकल्प्य विधानतः ।
वासुदेवः प्रधानस्तु ततः संकर्षणः स्वयम् ॥
2.48.m: having arranged [them] with the Deity-Gāyatrī according to rule, he should install [them]. / Vāsudeva is the principal, then Saṃkarṣaṇa himself,

2.48.s:
pradyumno hyaniruddhaśca mūrtibhedāstu vai prabhoḥ /
bahūni vividhānīha tasya śāpodbhavāni ca //
2.48.d:
प्रद्युम्नो ह्यनिरुद्धश्च मूर्तिभेदास्तु वै प्रभोः ।
बहूनि विविधानीह तस्य शापोद्भवानि च ॥
2.48.m: Pradyumna, and Aniruddha are indeed the different bodily forms of the Lord. / Many and diverse are His forms here that arose from curses,

2.48.s:
sarvāvarteṣu rūpāṇi jagatāṃ ca hitāya vai /
matsyaḥ kūrmo 'tha vārāho nārasiṃho 'tha vāmanaḥ //
2.48.d:
सर्वावर्तेषु रूपाणि जगतां च हिताय वै ।
मत्स्यः कूर्मो ऽथ वाराहो नारसिंहो ऽथ वामनः ॥
2.48.m: forms in all cosmic cycles, for the welfare of the worlds: / the Fish, the Tortoise, then the Boar, the Man-Lion, then the Dwarf,

2.48.s:
rāmo rāmaśca kṛṣṇaśca bauddhaḥ kalkī tathaiva ca /
tathānyāni na devasya hareḥ sāpodbhavāni ca //
2.48.d:
रामो रामश्च कृष्णश्च बौद्धः कल्की तथैव च ।
तथान्यानि न देवस्य हरेः सापोद्भवानि च ॥
2.48.m: Rāma, and Rāma, and Kṛṣṇa, the Buddha, and likewise Kalkin; / and there are other forms of the god Hari that did not arise from curses.

2.48.s:
teṣāmapi ca gāyatrīṃ kṛtvā stāpya ca pūjayet /
guhyāni devadevasya harernārāyaṇasya ca //
2.48.d:
तेषामपि च गायत्रीं कृत्वा स्ताप्य च पूजयेत् ।
गुह्यानि देवदेवस्य हरेर्नारायणस्य च ॥
2.48.m: Making a Gāyatrī for them too, installing and worshipping [them], / the secrets of the God of gods, Hari Nārāyaṇa,

2.48.s:
vijñānāni ca yantrāṇi mantropaniṣadāni ca /
pañca brahmāṅgajānīha pañcabhūtamayāni ca //
2.48.d:
विज्ञानानि च यन्त्राणि मन्त्रोपनिषदानि च ।
पञ्च ब्रह्माङ्गजानीह पञ्चभूतमयानि च ॥
2.48.m: the esoteric sciences, mystical diagrams, and mantra Upanisads, / five born of the limbs of Brahmā here, and consisting of the five gross elements:

2.48.s:
namo nārāyaṇāyeti mantraḥ paramaśobhanaḥ /
hareraṣṭākṣarāṇīha praṇavena samāsataḥ //
2.48.d:
नमो नारायणायेति मन्त्रः परमशोभनः ।
हरेरष्टाक्षराणीह प्रणवेन समासतः ॥
2.48.m: “Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa” is the supremely auspicious mantra; / here are the eight syllables of Hari, together with the Praṇava in brief:

2.48.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca /
pradyumnāya pradhānāya aniruddhāya vai namaḥ //
2.48.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय नमः संकर्षणाय च ।
प्रद्युम्नाय प्रधानाय अनिरुद्धाय वै नमः ॥
2.48.m: “Oṃ, obeisance to Vāsudeva, and obeisance to Saṃkarṣaṇa, / to Pradyumna the chief, and to Aniruddha, obeisance!”

2.48.s:
ekamekena mantreṇa sthāpayetparameśvaram /
biṃbāniyāni devasya śivasya parameṣṭhinaḥ //
2.48.d:
एकमेकेन मन्त्रेण स्थापयेत्परमेश्वरम् ।
बिंबानियानि देवस्य शिवस्य परमेष्ठिनः ॥
2.48.m: With each single mantra he should install the Supreme Lord. / Whatever icons of the god Śiva Parameṣṭhin [there are],

2.48.s:
pratiṣṭhā caiva pūjā ca liṅgavanmunisattamāḥ /
ratnavinyāsasahitaṃ kautukāni harerapi //
2.48.d:
प्रतिष्ठा चैव पूजा च लिङ्गवन्मुनिसत्तमाः ।
रत्नविन्याससहितं कौतुकानि हरेरपि ॥
2.48.m: their installation and worship are like that of the liṅga, O best of sages; / along with the deposit of gems, the auspicious rites of Hari too,

2.48.s:
acale kārayetsarvaṃ calepyevaṃ vidhānataḥ /
tannetronmīlanaṃ kuryānnetramantreṇa suvratāḥ //
2.48.d:
अचले कारयेत्सर्वं चलेप्येवं विधानतः ।
तन्नेत्रोन्मीलनं कुर्यान्नेत्रमन्त्रेण सुव्रताः ॥
2.48.m: he should perform everything for an immovable [icon], and likewise for a movable one according to rule. / He should perform the unclosing of its eyes with the eye-mantra, O men of good vows,

2.48.s:
kṣetrapradakṣiṇaṃ caiva ārāmasya purasya ca /
jalādhivāsanaṃ caiva pūrvavatparikīrtitam //
2.48.d:
क्षेत्रप्रदक्षिणं चैव आरामस्य पुरस्य च ।
जलाधिवासनं चैव पूर्ववत्परिकीर्तितम् ॥
2.48.m: and the circumambulation of the site, the garden, and the town, / and the dwelling in water is described as before.

2.48.s:
kuṇḍamaṇḍapanirmāṇaṃ śayanaṃ ca vidhīyate /
hutvā navāgnibhāgena navakuṇḍe yatāvidhi //
2.48.d:
कुण्डमण्डपनिर्माणं शयनं च विधीयते ।
हुत्वा नवाग्निभागेन नवकुण्डे यताविधि ॥
2.48.m: The preparation of the pit and pavilion, and the laying to rest are prescribed. / Having sacrificed according to rule in the nine pits with the nine-fire division,

2.48.s:
athavā pañcakuṇḍeṣu pradhāne kevale 'tha vā /
pratiṣṭhā kathitā divyā pāraṃparyakramāgatā //
2.48.d:
अथवा पञ्चकुण्डेषु प्रधाने केवले ऽथ वा ।
प्रतिष्ठा कथिता दिव्या पारंपर्यक्रमागता ॥
2.48.m: or in five pits, or in the chief one alone, / the divine installation handed down in succession of tradition is declared.

2.48.s:
śilodbhavānāṃ biṃbānāṃ citrābhāsasya vā punaḥ /
jalādhivāsanaṃ proktaṃ vṛṣendrasya prakīrtitam //
2.48.d:
शिलोद्भवानां बिंबानां चित्राभासस्य वा पुनः ।
जलाधिवासनं प्रोक्तं वृषेन्द्रस्य प्रकीर्तितम् ॥
2.48.m: For stone-made icons or for painted representations, / dwelling in water is declared; and it is proclaimed for the Lord of Bulls.

2.48.s:
prāsādasya pratiṣṭhāyāṃ pratiṣṭhā parikīrtitā /
prāsādāṅgasya sarvasya yathāṅgānāṃ tanoriva //
2.48.d:
प्रासादस्य प्रतिष्ठायां प्रतिष्ठा परिकीर्तिता ।
प्रासादाङ्गस्य सर्वस्य यथाङ्गानां तनोरिव ॥
2.48.m: In the installation of a temple, the installation of every constituent / of the temple is declared, just as of the limbs of a body.

2.48.s:
vṛṣāgnimātṛvighneśakumārānapi yatnataḥ /
śreṣṭhāṃ durgāṃ tathā caṇḍīṃ gāyatryā vai yathāvidhi //
2.48.d:
वृषाग्निमातृविघ्नेशकुमारानपि यत्नतः ।
श्रेष्ठां दुर्गां तथा चण्डीं गायत्र्या वै यथाविधि ॥
2.48.m: The Bull, Agni, the Mothers, Vighneśa, and Kumāra as well, carefully, / the supreme Durgā, and likewise Caṇḍī with the Gāyatrī, according to rule.

2.48.s:
prāgādyaṃ sthāpayecchaṃbhoraṣṭāvaraṇamuttamam /
lokapālagaṇeśādyānapi śaṃbhoḥ pravinyaset //
2.48.d:
प्रागाद्यं स्थापयेच्छंभोरष्टावरणमुत्तमम् ।
लोकपालगणेशाद्यानपि शंभोः प्रविन्यसेत् ॥
2.48.m: One should install Śambhu's excellent eight enclosures, beginning from the east; / one should also assign the guardians of the worlds, the lords of Gaṇas, and the others around Śambhu:

2.48.s:
umā caṇḍī ca nandī ca mahākālo mahāmuniḥ /
vighneśvaro mahābhṛṅgī skandaḥ saumyāditaḥ kramāt //
2.48.d:
उमा चण्डी च नन्दी च महाकालो महामुनिः ।
विघ्नेश्वरो महाभृङ्गी स्कन्दः सौम्यादितः क्रमात् ॥
2.48.m: Umā, Caṇḍī, Nandin, Mahākāla the great sage, / Vighneśvara, Mahābhṛṅgin, and Skanda, in order beginning from the north.

2.48.s:
indrādīnsveṣu sthāneṣu brahmāṇaṃ ca janārdanam /
sthāpayeccaiva yatnena kṣetreśaṃ veśagocare //
2.48.d:
इन्द्रादीन्स्वेषु स्थानेषु ब्रह्माणं च जनार्दनम् ।
स्थापयेच्चैव यत्नेन क्षेत्रेशं वेशगोचरे ॥
2.48.m: One should carefully install Indra and the others in their own places, and Brahmā and Janārdana, / and the guardian of the field within the range of the dwelling.

2.48.s:
siṃhāsane hyanantādīn vidyeśāmapi ca kramāt /
sthāpayetpraṇavenaiva guhyāṅgādīni paṅkaje //
2.48.d:
सिंहासने ह्यनन्तादीन् विद्येशामपि च क्रमात् ।
स्थापयेत्प्रणवेनैव गुह्याङ्गादीनि पङ्कजे ॥
2.48.m: Upon the lion-throne, one should install Ananta and the others, and the lords of wisdom in succession, / with the praṇava indeed, and the secret limbs and other [deities] upon the lotus.

2.48.s:
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktaṃ calasthāpanasuttamam /
sarveṣāmapi devānāṃ devīnāṃ ca viśeṣataḥ //
iti śrīliṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge 'ṣṭacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.48.d:
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तं चलस्थापनसुत्तमम् ।
सर्वेषामपि देवानां देवीनां च विशेषतः ॥
इति श्रीलिङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे ऽष्टचत्वारिंशो ऽध्यायः
2.48.m:
Thus, in brief, has been declared the excellent installation of movable [images] / of all gods, and especially of the goddesses.

Thus ends the forty-eighth chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Liṅgamahāpurāṇa.

2.49.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
aghoreśasya mahātmyaṃ bhavatā kathitaṃ purā /
pūjāṃ pratiṣṭhāṃ devasya bhagavanvaktumarhasi //
2.49.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
अघोरेशस्य महात्म्यं भवता कथितं पुरा ।
पूजां प्रतिष्ठां देवस्य भगवन्वक्तुमर्हसि ॥
2.49.m: The sages said: / The majesty of the lord Aghora was told by you formerly; / you ought to tell of the worship and installation of the god, O venerable one.

2.49.s:
sūta uvāca
aghoreṇāṅga yuktena vidhivacca viśeṣataḥ /
pratiṣṭhāliṅgavidhinā nānyatā munipuṅgavāḥ //
2.49.d:
सूत उवाच
अघोरेणाङ्ग युक्तेन विधिवच्च विशेषतः ।
प्रतिष्ठालिङ्गविधिना नान्यता मुनिपुङ्गवाः ॥
2.49.m: Sūta said: / With Aghora accompanied by the limbs, according to rule and in detail, / by the rule for the installation of a liṅga, not otherwise, O best of sages.

2.49.s:
tathāgnipūjāṃ vai kuryādyathā pūjā tathaiva ca /
sahasraṃ vā tadardhaṃ vā śatamaṣṭottaraṃ tu vā //
2.49.d:
तथाग्निपूजां वै कुर्याद्यथा पूजा तथैव च ।
सहस्रं वा तदर्धं वा शतमष्टोत्तरं तु वा ॥
2.49.m: In the same manner one should perform worship in fire, just as the worship [itself]; / a thousand [oblations], or half of that, or one hundred and eight.

2.49.s:
tilairhemaḥ prakartavyo dadhimadhvājyasaṃyutaiḥ /
ghṛtasaktumadūnāṃ ca sarvaduḥkhapramārjanam //
2.49.d:
तिलैर्हेमः प्रकर्तव्यो दधिमध्वाज्यसंयुतैः ।
घृतसक्तुमदूनां च सर्वदुःखप्रमार्जनम् ॥
2.49.m: The homa is to be performed with sesame seeds mixed with curd, honey, and clarified butter; / and [an oblation] of ghee, barley flour, and honey wipes away all grief.

2.49.s:
vyādhīnāṃ nāśanaṃ caiva tilahomastu bhūtidaḥ /
sahasreṇa mahābhūtiḥ śatena vyādhināśanam //
2.49.d:
व्याधीनां नाशनं चैव तिलहोमस्तु भूतिदः ।
सहस्रेण महाभूतिः शतेन व्याधिनाशनम् ॥
2.49.m: It destroys diseases, and a sesame homa grants prosperity; / with a thousand [oblations comes] great prosperity; with a hundred, destruction of disease.

2.49.s:
sarvaduḥkhavinirmukto japena ca na saṃśayaḥ /
aṣṭottaraśatenaiva trikāle ca yathāvidhi //
2.49.d:
सर्वदुःखविनिर्मुक्तो जपेन च न संशयः ।
अष्टोत्तरशतेनैव त्रिकाले च यथाविधि ॥
2.49.m: One is freed from all suffering by recitation, no doubt, / with one hundred and eight [recitations] at the three junctions of the day according to rule.

2.49.s:
aṣṭottarasahasreṇa ṣaṇmāsājjāyate dhruvam /
siddhayo naiva saṃdeho rājyamaṇḍālināmapi //
2.49.d:
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रेण षण्मासाज्जायते ध्रुवम् ।
सिद्धयो नैव संदेहो राज्यमण्डालिनामपि ॥
2.49.m: With one thousand and eight, surely after six months / perfections arise—there is no doubt—even for rulers of kingdoms.

2.49.s:
sahasreṇa jvaro yāti kṣīreṇa ca juhoti yam /
trikālaṃ māsamekaṃ tu sahasraṃ juhuyātpayaḥ //
2.49.d:
सहस्रेण ज्वरो याति क्षीरेण च जुहोति यम् ।
त्रिकालं मासमेकं तु सहस्रं जुहुयात्पयः ॥
2.49.m: With a thousand, fever departs when one offers milk in oblation; / at the three junctions of the day for one month, one should offer a thousand oblations of milk.

2.49.s:
māsena siddhyate tasya mahāsaubhāgyamuttamam /
siddhyate cābdahomena kṣaudrājyadadhisaṃyutam //
2.49.d:
मासेन सिद्ध्यते तस्य महासौभाग्यमुत्तमम् ।
सिद्ध्यते चाब्दहोमेन क्षौद्राज्यदधिसंयुतम् ॥
2.49.m: In a month, excellent great good fortune is accomplished for him; / and it is accomplished by a year-long homa [of oblations] combined with honey, clarified butter, and curd.

2.49.s:
yavakṣīrājyahomena jātitaṇḍulakena vā /
prīyeta bhagavānīśo hyaghoraḥ parameśvaraḥ //
2.49.d:
यवक्षीराज्यहोमेन जातितण्डुलकेन वा ।
प्रीयेत भगवानीशो ह्यघोरः परमेश्वरः ॥
2.49.m: By a homa of barley, milk, and clarified butter, or with wild rice, / the lord Īśa, Aghora the Parameśvara, is pleased.

2.49.s:
dadhnā puṣṭirnṛpāṇāṃ ca kṣīrahomena śāntikam /
ṣaṇmāsaṃ tu ghṛtaṃ hutvā sarvavyādhivināśanam //
2.49.d:
दध्ना पुष्टिर्नृपाणां च क्षीरहोमेन शान्तिकम् ।
षण्मासं तु घृतं हुत्वा सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् ॥
2.49.m: With curd comes nourishment for kings; by a milk-homa comes pacification; / and having offered clarified butter for six months, all diseases are destroyed.

2.49.s:
rājayakṣmā tilairhemānnaśyate vatsareṇa tu /
yavahomena cāyuṣyaṃ ghṛtena ca jayastadā //
2.49.d:
राजयक्ष्मा तिलैर्हेमान्नश्यते वत्सरेण तु ।
यवहोमेन चायुष्यं घृतेन च जयस्तदा ॥
2.49.m: Consumption is destroyed in a year by oblations of sesame; / and by a homa of barley comes long life, and by clarified butter then comes victory.

2.49.s:
sarvakuṣṭhakṣayārthaṃ ca madhunāktaiśca taṇḍulaiḥ /
juhuyādayutaṃ nityaṃ ṣaṇmāsānniyataḥ sadā //
2.49.d:
सर्वकुष्ठक्षयार्थं च मधुनाक्तैश्च तण्डुलैः ।
जुहुयादयुतं नित्यं षण्मासान्नियतः सदा ॥
2.49.m: And for the destruction of all leprosy, with grains smeared with honey, / one should offer ten thousand [oblations] daily for six months, always restrained.

2.49.s:
ājyaṅkṣīraṃ madhuścaiva madhuratrayamucyate /
samastaṃ tuṣyate tasya nāśayedvai bhagandaram //
2.49.d:
आज्यङ्क्षीरं मधुश्चैव मधुरत्रयमुच्यते ।
समस्तं तुष्यते तस्य नाशयेद्वै भगन्दरम् ॥
2.49.m: Clarified butter, milk, and honey are called the three sweets; / all is satisfied for him, and it destroys fistula.

2.49.s:
kevalaṃ ghṛtahomena sarvarogakṣayaḥ smṛtaḥ /
sarvavyādhi haraṃ dhyānaṃ sthāpanaṃ vidhinārcanam //
2.49.d:
केवलं घृतहोमेन सर्वरोगक्षयः स्मृतः ।
सर्वव्याधि हरं ध्यानं स्थापनं विधिनार्चनम् ॥
2.49.m: By a homa of clarified butter alone, destruction of all diseases is remembered; / meditation, installation, and ritual worship according to rule remove all sickness.

2.49.s:
evaṃ saṃkṣepataḥ proktamaghorasya mahātmanaḥ /
pratiṣṭhā yajanaṃ sarvaṃ nandinā kathitaṃ purā //
2.49.d:
एवं संक्षेपतः प्रोक्तमघोरस्य महात्मनः ।
प्रतिष्ठा यजनं सर्वं नन्दिना कथितं पुरा ॥
2.49.m: Thus, in brief, has been declared the installation and all the worship / of the great-souled Aghora, told formerly by Nandin

2.49.s:
brahmaputrāya śiṣyāya tena vyāsāya suvratāḥ //
śrīlīṅgamahāpurāṇe uttarabhāge ekonapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ
2.49.d:
ब्रह्मपुत्राय शिष्याय तेन व्यासाय सुव्रताः ॥
श्रीलीङ्गमहापुराणे उत्तरभागे एकोनपञ्चाशत्तमो ऽध्यायः
2.49.m:
to the son of Brahmā, his disciple, and by him to Vyāsa, O men of good vows.

Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter in the Uttarabhāga of the glorious Liṅgamahāpurāṇa.

2.50.s:
ṛṣaya ūcuḥ
nigrahaḥ kathitastena śivavaktreṇa śūlinā /
kṛtāparāndhināṃ taṃ tu vaktumarhasi suvrata //
2.50.d:
ऋषय ऊचुः
निग्रहः कथितस्तेन शिववक्त्रेण शूलिना ।
कृतापरान्धिनां तं तु वक्तुमर्हसि सुव्रत ॥
2.50.m: The sages said: / Restraining power was spoken of by that trident-bearing Śiva with his mouth / against those who commit offenses; you ought to speak of it, O you of good vows.

2.50.s:
tvayā navidinaṃ nāsti laukikaṃ vaidikaṃ tathā /
śrautaṃ smārtaṃ mahābhāga romaharṣaṇa suvrata //
2.50.d:
त्वया नविदिनं नास्ति लौकिकं वैदिकं तथा ।
श्रौतं स्मार्तं महाभाग रोमहर्षण सुव्रत ॥
2.50.m: Nothing is unknown to you, worldly or Vedic, / Śrauta or Smārta, O highly fortunate one, Romaharṣaṇa of good vows.

2.50.s:
sūta uvāca
purā bhṛgusutenokto hiraṇyākṣāya suvratāḥ /
nigraho 'ghoraśiṣyeṇa śukreṇākṣayatejasā //
2.50.d:
सूत उवाच
पुरा भृगुसुतेनोक्तो हिरण्याक्षाय सुव्रताः ।
निग्रहो ऽघोरशिष्येण शुक्रेणाक्षयतेजसा ॥
2.50.m: Sūta said: / Formerly, O men of good vows, restraining power was declared to Hiraṇyākṣa / by Bhṛgu's son Śukra of imperishable splendor, the disciple of Aghora.

2.50.s:
tasya prasādaddaityendro hiraṇyākṣaḥ pratāpavān /
trailokyamakhilaṃ jitvā sadevāsuramānuṣam //
2.50.d:
तस्य प्रसादद्दैत्येन्द्रो हिरण्याक्षः प्रतापवान् ।
त्रैलोक्यमखिलं जित्वा सदेवासुरमानुषम् ॥
2.50.m: By his grace, the mighty lord of Daityas, Hiraṇyākṣa, / having conquered the entire threefold world along with gods, Asuras, and mortals,

2.50.s:
utpādya putraṃ gaṇapaṃ cāndhakaṃ cāruvikramam /
rarāja loke devena varāheṇa niṣūditaḥ //
2.50.d:
उत्पाद्य पुत्रं गणपं चान्धकं चारुविक्रमम् ।
रराज लोके देवेन वराहेण निषूदितः ॥
2.50.m: and having begotten a son, the lord of Gaṇas, Andhaka of beautiful valour, / shone in the world, [until] he was slain by the god Varāha.

2.50.s:
strībādhāṃ bālabādhāṃ ca gavāmapi viśeṣataḥ /
kurvato nāsti vijayo mārgeṇānena bhūtale //
2.50.d:
स्त्रीबाधां बालबाधां च गवामपि विशेषतः ।
कुर्वतो नास्ति विजयो मार्गेणानेन भूतले ॥
2.50.m: For one who causes harm to women, harm to children, and especially to cows, / there is no victory on earth by this path.

2.50.s:
tena daityena sā devī dharā nītā rasātalam /
tenāghoreṇa devena niṣphalo nigrahaḥ kṛtaḥ //
2.50.d:
तेन दैत्येन सा देवी धरा नीता रसातलम् ।
तेनाघोरेण देवेन निष्फलो निग्रहः कृतः ॥
2.50.m: By that Daitya, that goddess Earth was carried to the netherworld; / therefore by the god Aghora his restraining power was rendered fruitless.

2.50.s:
saṃvatsara sahasrānte varāheṇa ca sūditaḥ /
tasmādaghorasiddhyarthaṃ brāhmaṇānnaiva bādhayet //
2.50.d:
संवत्सर सहस्रान्ते वराहेण च सूदितः ।
तस्मादघोरसिद्ध्यर्थं ब्राह्मणान्नैव बाधयेत् ॥
2.50.m: And at the end of a thousand years he was slain by Varāha; / therefore, for the success of Aghora, one should never torment brāhmaṇas;

2.50.s:
strīṇāmapi viśeṣeṇa gavāmapi na kārayet /
guhyādguhyatamaṅgopyamatiguhyaṃ vadāmi vaḥ //
2.50.d:
स्त्रीणामपि विशेषेण गवामपि न कारयेत् ।
गुह्याद्गुह्यतमङ्गोप्यमतिगुह्यं वदामि वः ॥
2.50.m: especially to women, and also to cows, one should cause no harm. / The most secret of secrets, to be hidden, extremely secret, I tell you:

2.50.s:
ātatāyinamuddiśya kartavyaṃ nṛpasattamaiḥ /
brāhmaṇebhyo na kartavyaṃ svarāṣṭreśasya vā punaḥ //
2.50.d:
आततायिनमुद्दिश्य कर्तव्यं नृपसत्तमैः ।
ब्राह्मणेभ्यो न कर्तव्यं स्वराष्ट्रेशस्य वा पुनः ॥
2.50.m: It should be performed by the best of kings directed against a deadly assailant; / it should not be performed against brāhmaṇas, or again against the ruler of one's own realm.

2.50.s:
atīvadurjaye prāpte bale sarve niṣūdite /
adharmayuddhe saṃprāpte kuryādvidhimanuttamam //
2.50.d:
अतीवदुर्जये प्राप्ते बले सर्वे निषूदिते ।
अधर्मयुद्धे संप्राप्ते कुर्याद्विधिमनुत्तमम् ॥
2.50.m: When an exceedingly invincible army is encountered and all is destroyed, / when an unrighteous battle has arrived, one should perform the unsurpassed rite.

2.50.s:
aghṛṇenaiva kartavyo hyaghṛṇenaiva kārayet /
kṛtamātre na saṃdeho nigrahaḥ saṃprajāyate //
2.50.d:
अघृणेनैव कर्तव्यो ह्यघृणेनैव कारयेत् ।
कृतमात्रे न संदेहो निग्रहः संप्रजायते ॥
2.50.m: It should only be performed by one without pity, and one should cause it to be performed only by one without pity; / as soon as it is performed, restraint arises without doubt.

2.50.s:
lakṣamātraṃ pumāñjaptvā aghoraṃ ghorarūpiṇam /
daśāṃśaṃ vidhinā hutvā tilena dvijasattamāḥ //
2.50.d:
लक्षमात्रं पुमाञ्जप्त्वा अघोरं घोररूपिणम् ।
दशांशं विधिना हुत्वा तिलेन द्विजसत्तमाः ॥
2.50.m: A man, having recited only one hundred thousand times [the mantra of] Aghora of terrible form, / and having offered a tenth part according to rule with sesame, O best of the twice-born,

2.50.s:
saṃpūjya lakṣapuṣpeṇa sitena vidhipūrvakam /
bāṇaliṅge 'thavā vahnau dakṣiṇāmūrtimāśritaḥ //
2.50.d:
संपूज्य लक्षपुष्पेण सितेन विधिपूर्वकम् ।
बाणलिङ्गे ऽथवा वह्नौ दक्षिणामूर्तिमाश्रितः ॥
2.50.m: and having worshipped with one hundred thousand white flowers according to rule, / in a bāṇaliṅga or in fire, taking refuge in Dakṣiṇāmūrti,

2.50.s:
siddhamantro 'nyatā nāsti draṣṭā siddhyādayaḥ punaḥ /
siddhamantraḥ svayaṃ kuryātpretasthāne viśeṣataḥ //
2.50.d:
सिद्धमन्त्रो ऽन्यता नास्ति द्रष्टा सिद्ध्यादयः पुनः ।
सिद्धमन्त्रः स्वयं कुर्यात्प्रेतस्थाने विशेषतः ॥
2.50.m: his mantra becomes perfected, not otherwise; he will see perfections and the rest. / One whose mantra is perfected should himself perform it, especially in a cremation ground,

2.50.s:
mātṛsthāne 'pi vā vidvānvedavedāṅgapāragaḥ /
kevalaṃ mantrasiddho vā brāhmaṇaḥ śivabhāvitaḥ //
2.50.d:
मातृस्थाने ऽपि वा विद्वान्वेदवेदाङ्गपारगः ।
केवलं मन्त्रसिद्धो वा ब्राह्मणः शिवभावितः ॥
2.50.m: or in a temple of the Mothers, being wise and versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / or a brāhmaṇa whose mantra alone is perfected and who is devoted to Śiva.

2.50.s:
kuryādvidhimimaṃ dhīmānātmanor'thaṃ nṛpasya vā /
sūlāṣṭakaṃ nyasedvidvānpūrvādīśānakāntakam //
2.50.d:
कुर्याद्विधिमिमं धीमानात्मनोर्ऽथं नृपस्य वा ।
सूलाष्टकं न्यसेद्विद्वान्पूर्वादीशानकान्तकम् ॥
2.50.m: A wise man should perform this rite for his own sake or for a king's; / the wise one should install eight tridents, beginning from the east and ending with Īśāna:

2.50.s:
triśikhaṃ ca triśūlaṃ ca caturviśācchikāgrataḥ /
aghoravigrahaṃ kṛtvā saṃkalīkṛtavigrahaḥ //
2.50.d:
त्रिशिखं च त्रिशूलं च चतुर्विशाच्छिकाग्रतः ।
अघोरविग्रहं कृत्वा संकलीकृतविग्रहः ॥
2.50.m: having three crests and being a trident, twenty-four [aṅgulas] to the tip of the crest. / Having visualized the form of Aghora, having his own body ritually composed,

2.50.s:
sarvanāśakaraṃ dhyātvā sarvakarmāṇi kārayet /
kālāgnikoṭisaṃkāśaṃ svadehamapi bhāvayet //
2.50.d:
सर्वनाशकरं ध्यात्वा सर्वकर्माणि कारयेत् ।
कालाग्निकोटिसंकाशं स्वदेहमपि भावयेत् ॥
2.50.m: having meditated on him who causes the destruction of all, he should perform all rites; / he should also imagine his own body as resembling ten million fires of time,

2.50.s:
śūlaṃ kapālaṃ pāśaṃ ca daṇḍaṃ caiva śarāsanam /
bāṇaṃ ḍamarukaṃ khaḍgamaṣṭāyudhamanukramāt //
2.50.d:
शूलं कपालं पाशं च दण्डं चैव शरासनम् ।
बाणं डमरुकं खड्गमष्टायुधमनुक्रमात् ॥
2.50.m: holding a trident, a skull-bowl, a noose, a staff, a bow, / an arrow, an hourglass drum, and a sword—eight weapons in succession,

2.50.s:
aṣṭahastaśca varado nīlakaṇṭho digaṃbaraḥ /
pañcatattvasamārūḍho hyardhacandradharaḥ prabhuḥ //
2.50.d:
अष्टहस्तश्च वरदो नीलकण्ठो दिगंबरः ।
पञ्चतत्त्वसमारूढो ह्यर्धचन्द्रधरः प्रभुः ॥
2.50.m: eight-armed, granting boons, blue-throated, sky-clad, / mounted upon the five principles, the lord bearing the crescent moon,

2.50.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālavadano raudradṛṣṭirbhayaṅkaraḥ /
huṃphaṭkāramahāśabdaśabditākhiladiṅmukhaḥ //
2.50.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालवदनो रौद्रदृष्टिर्भयङ्करः ।
हुंफट्कारमहाशब्दशब्दिताखिलदिङ्मुखः ॥
2.50.m: with a face terrible with fangs, of wrathful gaze, terrifying, / making all the quarters resound with the great sound of huṃ and phaṭ,

2.50.s:
trinetraṃ nāgapāśena subaddhamukuṭaṃ svayam /
sarvābharaṇasaṃpannaṃ pretabhasmāvaguṇṭhitam //
2.50.d:
त्रिनेत्रं नागपाशेन सुबद्धमुकुटं स्वयम् ।
सर्वाभरणसंपन्नं प्रेतभस्मावगुण्ठितम् ॥
2.50.m: three-eyed, himself with a crown firmly bound with a serpent-noose, / endowed with all ornaments, smeared with the ashes of corpses,

2.50.s:
bhūtaiḥ pretaiḥ piśācaiśca ḍākinībhiśca rākṣasaiḥ /
saṃvṛtaṃ gajakṛttvā ca sarpabhūṣaṇabhūṣitam //
2.50.d:
भूतैः प्रेतैः पिशाचैश्च डाकिनीभिश्च राक्षसैः ।
संवृतं गजकृत्त्वा च सर्पभूषणभूषितम् ॥
2.50.m: surrounded by Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Ḍākinīs, and Rākṣasas, / clad in an elephant hide, adorned with serpent ornaments,

2.50.s:
vṛścikābharaṇaṃ devaṃ nīlanīradanisvanam /
nīlāñjanādrisaṃkāśaṃ siṃhacarmottarīyakam //
2.50.d:
वृश्चिकाभरणं देवं नीलनीरदनिस्वनम् ।
नीलाञ्जनाद्रिसंकाशं सिंहचर्मोत्तरीयकम् ॥
2.50.m: the god whose ornaments are scorpions, sounding like a dark raincloud, / resembling a mountain of black collyrium, with an upper garment of lion skin.

2.50.s:
dhyāyedevamaghoreśaṃ ghoraghorataraṃ śivam /
ṣaṭtriṃśaduktamātrābhiḥ prāṇāyāmena suvratāḥ //
2.50.d:
ध्यायेदेवमघोरेशं घोरघोरतरं शिवम् ।
षट्त्रिंशदुक्तमात्राभिः प्राणायामेन सुव्रताः ॥
2.50.m:
Possessed of the great mudrā, one should perform all the rites,
either in the fire of a funeral pyre or in a cremation ground, according to rule, having perfected the mantra.

2.50.s:
mahāmudrāsamāyuktaḥ sarvakarmāṇi kārayet /
siddhamantraścitāgnau vā pretasthāne yathāvidhi //
2.50.d:
महामुद्रासमायुक्तः सर्वकर्माणि कारयेत् ।
सिद्धमन्त्रश्चिताग्नौ वा प्रेतस्थाने यथाविधि ॥
2.50.m:
He should establish [fire-pits] in the centre, in the east, south, and west,
and in the north, duly making fire-pits according to the scriptures.

2.50.s:
sthāpayenmadhyadeśe tu eendre yāmye ca vāruṇe /
kauberyāṃ vidivatkṛtvā homakuṇḍāni śāstrataḥ //
2.50.d:
स्थापयेन्मध्यदेशे तु एएन्द्रे याम्ये च वारुणे ।
कौबेर्यां विदिवत्कृत्वा होमकुण्डानि शास्त्रतः ॥
2.50.m:
The preceptor [should sit] at the central pit, and the practitioners in the directions;
having strewn [the sacred grass] in reverse order, as before, bearing a trident,

2.50.s:
ācāryo madhyakuṇḍe tu sādhakāśca diśāsu vai /
paristīrya vilomena pūrvavacchūlasaṃbhṛtaḥ //
2.50.d:
आचार्यो मध्यकुण्डे तु साधकाश्च दिशासु वै ।
परिस्तीर्य विलोमेन पूर्ववच्छूलसंभृतः ॥
2.50.m:
seated in the centre of the pedestal of the Fire of Time, he himself and disciples of like character,
having meditated upon terrible Aghoreśa accompanied by the thirty-two-syllabled [mantra],

2.50.s:
kālāgnipīṭhamadhyasthaḥ svayaṃ śiṣyaiśca tādṛśaiḥ /
dhyātvā ghoramaghoreśaṃ dvātriṃśākṣarasaṃyutam //
2.50.d:
कालाग्निपीठमध्यस्थः स्वयं शिष्यैश्च तादृशैः ।
ध्यात्वा घोरमघोरेशं द्वात्रिंशाक्षरसंयुतम् ॥
2.50.m:
having made [an effigy] of vibhītaka wood measuring twelve finger-breadths,
placing it upon the seat, with charcoal [drawing] the enemy of the king—

2.50.s:
vibhītakena vai kṛtvā dvādaśāṅgulamānataḥ /
pīṭhe nyasya nṛpendrasya śatrumaṅgārakeṇa tu //
2.50.d:
विभीतकेन वै कृत्वा द्वादशाङ्गुलमानतः ।
पीठे न्यस्य नृपेन्द्रस्य शत्रुमङ्गारकेण तु ॥
2.50.m:
the brāhmaṇa, overcome with anger, should bury the enemy beneath the pit,
face-downward with feet turned upward, carefully in all the pits.

2.50.s:
kuṇḍasyādhaḥ khanecchatruṃ brāhmaṇaḥ krodhamūrcchitaḥ /
adhomukhordhvapādaṃ tu sarvakuṇḍeṣu yatnataḥ //
2.50.d:
कुण्डस्याधः खनेच्छत्रुं ब्राह्मणः क्रोधमूर्च्छितः ।
अधोमुखोर्ध्वपादं तु सर्वकुण्डेषु यत्नतः ॥
2.50.m:
Bringing charcoal from the cremation ground, he should burn it along with chaff;
there, silently, the practitioner dedicated to celibacy should establish the fire.

2.50.s:
śmaśānāṅgāramānīya tuṣeṇa saha dāhayet /
tatrāgniṃ sthāpayettūṣṇīṃ brahmacaryaparāyaṇaḥ //
2.50.d:
श्मशानाङ्गारमानीय तुषेण सह दाहयेत् ।
तत्राग्निं स्थापयेत्तूष्णीं ब्रह्मचर्यपरायणः ॥
2.50.m:
Then with the Māyūra weapon he should kindle the blaze in the navel;
with the shed skin of a snake, accompanied by chaff and cotton mixed with bone,

2.50.s:
māyūrāstreṇa nābhyāṃ tu jvalanaṃ dīpayettataḥ /
kañcukaṃ tuṣasaṃyuktaiḥ kārpāsāsthisamanvitaiḥ //
2.50.d:
मायूरास्त्रेण नाभ्यां तु ज्वलनं दीपयेत्ततः ।
कञ्चुकं तुषसंयुक्तैः कार्पासास्थिसमन्वितैः ॥
2.50.m:
and especially mixed with gold-substances together with red cloth,
he should perform the oblation with oils extracted by hand-presses.

2.50.s:
raktavastrasamaṃ miśrairhemadravyairviśeṣataḥ /
hastayantrodbhavaistailaiḥ saha homaṃ tu kārayet //
2.50.d:
रक्तवस्त्रसमं मिश्रैर्हेमद्रव्यैर्विशेषतः ।
हस्तयन्त्रोद्भवैस्तैलैः सह होमं तु कारयेत् ॥
2.50.m:
He should offer one thousand and eight oblations in succession,
starting properly on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight,

2.50.s:
aṣṭottarasahasraṃ tu homayedanupūrvaśaḥ /
kṛṣṇapakṣe caturdaśyāṃ samārabhya yathākramam //
2.50.d:
अष्टोत्तरसहस्रं तु होमयेदनुपूर्वशः ।
कृष्णपक्षे चतुर्दश्यां समारभ्य यथाक्रमम् ॥
2.50.m:
up to the eighth day, avoiding the place of the charcoal circle.
When this is done, the enemies of the king, along with their kin,

2.50.s:
aṣṭamyantaṃ tathāṅgāramaṇḍalasthānavarjitaḥ /
evaṃ kṛte nṛpendrasya śatravaḥ kulajaiḥ saha //
2.50.d:
अष्टम्यन्तं तथाङ्गारमण्डलस्थानवर्जितः ।
एवं कृते नृपेन्द्रस्य शत्रवः कुलजैः सह ॥
2.50.m:
afflicted with all sorrows, go to the abode of Yama.
And with this mantra, taking a fingernail in a human skull,

2.50.s:
sarvaduḥkhasamopetāḥ prayānti yamasādanam /
mantreṇānena cādāya nṛkapāle nakhaṃ tathā //
2.50.d:
सर्वदुःखसमोपेताः प्रयान्ति यमसादनम् ।
मन्त्रेणानेन चादाय नृकपाले नखं तथा ॥
2.50.m:
and the hair of men, charcoal, chaff, and snake-skin,
a shred of rag, dust from the royal road, or from the sweeping of a house,

2.50.s:
keśaṃ nṛṇāṃ tathāṅgāraṃ tuṣaṃ kañcukameva ca /
cīracchaṭāṃ rājadhūlīṃ gṛhasaṃmārjanasya vā //
2.50.d:
केशं नृणां तथाङ्गारं तुषं कञ्चुकमेव च ।
चीरच्छटां राजधूलीं गृहसंमार्जनस्य वा ॥
2.50.m:
the teeth of a venomous snake, the teeth of a bull,
and of cows successively, and the teeth and claws of a tiger,

2.50.s:
viṣasarpasya dantāni vṛṣadantāni yāni tu /
gavāṃ caiva krameṇaiva vyāghradantanakhāni ca //
2.50.d:
विषसर्पस्य दन्तानि वृषदन्तानि यानि तु ।
गवां चैव क्रमेणैव व्याघ्रदन्तनखानि च ॥
2.50.m:
and likewise of black antelopes, and of a cat as before,
and the teeth of a mongoose, and especially of a boar,

2.50.s:
tathā kṛṣṇamṛgāṇāṃ ca biḍālasya ca pūrvavat /
nakulasya ca dantāni varāhasya viśeṣataḥ //
2.50.d:
तथा कृष्णमृगाणां च बिडालस्य च पूर्ववत् ।
नकुलस्य च दन्तानि वराहस्य विशेषतः ॥
2.50.m:
having prepared the fangs, O men of good vows, with this mantra,
he should mutter the supreme Aghora mantra one hundred and eight times.

2.50.s:
daṃṣṭrāṇi sādhayitvā tu mantreṇānena suvratāḥ /
japedaṣṭottaraśataṃ mantraṃ cāghoramuttamam //
2.50.d:
दंष्ट्राणि साधयित्वा तु मन्त्रेणानेन सुव्रताः ।
जपेदष्टोत्तरशतं मन्त्रं चाघोरमुत्तमम् ॥
2.50.m:
He should wrap that skull and nail in a shroud from a corpse,
in a field, a house, a town, a cremation ground, or a kingdom,

2.50.s:
tatkapālaṃ nakhaṃ kṣetre gṛhe vā nagare 'pi vā /
pretasthāne 'pi vā rāṣṭre mṛtavastreṇa veṣṭayet //
2.50.d:
तत्कपालं नखं क्षेत्रे गृहे वा नगरे ऽपि वा ।
प्रेतस्थाने ऽपि वा राष्ट्रे मृतवस्त्रेण वेष्टयेत् ॥
2.50.m:
when [the moon enters] the eighth zodiacal sign of the enemy, or when a halo surrounds the sun,
or when a halo surrounds the moon, with this mantra, O men of good vows.

2.50.s:
śatroraṣṭamārāśau vā pariviṣṭe divākare /
some vā pariviṣṭe tu mantreṇānena suvratāḥ //
2.50.d:
शत्रोरष्टमाराशौ वा परिविष्टे दिवाकरे ।
सोमे वा परिविष्टे तु मन्त्रेणानेन सुव्रताः ॥
2.50.m:
Destruction of his position occurs, and the destruction of the enemy takes place.
Having drawn the king's enemy standing in departure,

2.50.s:
sthānanāśo bhavettasya śatrornāśaśca jāyate /
śatruṃ rājñaḥ samālikhya gamane samavasthite //
2.50.d:
स्थाननाशो भवेत्तस्य शत्रोर्नाशश्च जायते ।
शत्रुं राज्ञः समालिख्य गमने समवस्थिते ॥
2.50.m:
upon the ground resembling a mirror, adorned under a canopy,
endowed with four arched gateways, encircled with garlands of darbha grass,

2.50.s:
